abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.name: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.scope: screening recommendations (men 65-75 who smoked), ultrasound imaging, surveillance intervals, elective repair thresholds, rupture
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.core: Older adult with abdominal aortic dilation may remain asymptomatic until expansion or rupture; sudden abdominal/back pain and hypotension require immediate vascular rescue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking strongest modifiable risk; older age, male sex, family history, hypertension, atherosclerosis
Women have higher rupture risk at smaller diameters; most aneurysms infrarenal
Existing AAA: **diameter and high BP** predict rupture; cholesterol, A1c do not

rows.label: Clues
items: Incidental pulsatile expansile abdominal mass; localized persistent pain suggests symptomatic aneurysm
Rupture triad incompletely present; transient stability may reflect contained retroperitoneal hemorrhage
Blue toe/distal ischemia may result from mural thrombus embolization
Acute back pain unchanged by movement = **referred pain**; prevertebral calcification on x-ray; not disc disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Medial elastin/collagen degradation → progressive enlargement; greater wall radius increases tension

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Abdominal ultrasound** diagnoses AAA, generally diameter ≥3 cm; no contrast required
★ Stable suspected rupture or preoperative planning → **CT angiography**
Unstable suspected rupture → bedside ultrasound if immediate; no CT transport delaying surgery
Ultrasound detects aneurysm but cannot reliably exclude rupture; follow symptoms/hemodynamics

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Rupture → **urgent vascular repair**, IV access, blood products; avoid delaying for complete workup
Permissive hypotension during transfer/resuscitation until hemorrhage control when clinically feasible
★ Elective repair: **≥5.5 cm men, ≥5.0 cm women**, symptoms; **not if short life expectancy** (metastatic cancer)
Rapid growth ≥0.5 cm/6 months → repair consideration; endovascular versus open based on anatomy/fitness
Smaller asymptomatic lesions → ultrasound surveillance below; refer vascular surgery, manage cardiovascular risks

rows.label: Complications
items: Rupture, thrombosis, distal embolization; repair → AKI, bowel ischemia, endoleak after EVAR
Aortoenteric fistula after prior graft: herald GI bleed → catastrophic hemorrhage; urgent evaluation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **one-time ultrasound men 65–75 who ever smoked**; selectively screen never-smoking men
Women never smoked/no family history → no screening; women smokers/family history → USPSTF evidence insufficient
Smoking cessation, BP control, statin for atherosclerotic disease; lifelong imaging follow-up after EVAR

rows.label: Mimics
items: Renal colic: flank-to-groin pain, hematuria; shock atypical
Aortic dissection: abrupt chest/back pain, possible pulse deficits or branch ischemia

abdominal-trauma.name: Abdominal trauma
abdominal-trauma.scope: Blunt abdominal trauma (splenic/hepatic laceration, FAST exam, CT scan), penetrating abdominal trauma (stab, gunshot, peritonitis, exploratory laparotomy indications)
abdominal-trauma.core: Abdominal injury after collision, fall, stabbing, or gunshot: hemodynamic status and peritoneal signs determine imaging versus immediate operation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: High-speed deceleration, seat-belt compression, lower rib fractures; anticoagulation increases bleeding risk
Stab wounds may spare viscera; bullets frequently injure multiple structures

rows.label: Clues
items: LUQ pain or referred left shoulder pain → splenic injury; RUQ tenderness → hepatic injury
Distention, ecchymoses, abdominal wall marks; initially benign examination does not exclude bowel injury
★ **Rigidity, rebound, persistent hypotension**, or evisceration → urgent operative assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Solid-organ disruption → intraperitoneal hemorrhage; mesenteric injury → ischemia or delayed perforation
Retroperitoneal injury may produce little intraperitoneal free fluid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **FAST** at bedside during resuscitation; detects free fluid, not organ-specific injury
★ Stable → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**; evaluate solid organs, bowel, retroperitoneum
Negative FAST with ongoing shock → search thorax/pelvis, repeat assessment; do not assume safety
Stable anterior stab → local wound exploration or serial examination/CT; trajectory guides evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway, large-bore IV access, warmed blood products; massive transfusion for hemorrhagic shock
★ Unstable + positive FAST, peritonitis, or ongoing transfusion need → **exploratory laparotomy**; no CT delay
Stable splenic/hepatic injury → monitored nonoperative care; blush, transient response → angioembolization (older questions: laparotomy)
Enteric contents, uncontrolled bleeding → operation; transperitoneal gunshot → **laparotomy** even if stable; selected stabs observed
Suspected bowel perforation → ceftriaxone + metronidazole, trauma surgery; free subdiaphragmatic air → **laparotomy**, no CT

rows.label: Complications
items: Delayed splenic rupture, abscess, bile leak, abdominal compartment syndrome
Missed hollow-viscus injury → sepsis; splenectomy → overwhelming encapsulated bacterial infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Restraints, airbags, injury-prevention counseling
★ After splenectomy → **pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib vaccines**; fever requires urgent antibiotics

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pelvic hemorrhage: unstable pelvis, negative abdominal FAST
Tension pneumothorax: unilateral absent breath sounds, obstructive shock

abdominal-trauma.evidence: Not checked online; established trauma assessment and management principles.

abdominal-wall-disorders.name: Abdominal wall disorders
abdominal-wall-disorders.scope: Rectus sheath hematoma, Fothergill sign, epigastric hernia, umbilical hernia, incisional hernia, diastasis recti
abdominal-wall-disorders.core: A focal abdominal-wall mass or pain persisting with muscle contraction suggests a wall lesion rather than visceral disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Anticoagulation, severe cough, pregnancy, trauma → rectus bleeding
Prior laparotomy, obesity, wound infection → incisional defect; increased intra-abdominal pressure promotes hernias

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Fothergill sign**: palpable rectus mass remains fixed during contraction, does not cross midline
Carnett sign: tenderness unchanged/increased with tensing supports abdominal-wall pain
★ Irreducibility with pain, vomiting, skin discoloration → incarceration/strangulation
Diastasis: broad midline ridge with head raising; intact fascia, no incarceration

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Epigastric vessel or muscle injury → blood confined within rectus sheath
Fascial defect permits fat/bowel protrusion; linea alba stretching separates rectus muscles in diastasis

rows.label: Dx
items: Standing examination with Valsalva; assess reducibility, obstruction and peritoneal signs
★ Suspected hematoma → **CBC, coagulation studies, CT**; contrast identifies active extravasation
Ultrasound for uncertain superficial hernia; CT for complex postoperative anatomy or bowel compromise

rows.label: Tx
items: Stable hematoma → analgesia, observation, hold/reverse anticoagulation when bleeding warrants
★ Hemodynamic instability → resuscitation/transfusion; persistent arterial bleeding → **embolization**
Strangulated or obstructed hernia → urgent operation; avoid forceful reduction
Symptomatic adult hernia → elective repair; diastasis → reassurance, core rehabilitation

rows.label: Complications
items: Hematoma → anemia, hemorrhagic shock; operative exploration can disrupt tamponade
Hernia → bowel ischemia/perforation; repair → infection or recurrence

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight management, smoking cessation, constipation/cough control; careful anticoagulant monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Appendicitis: visceral/peritoneal findings, pain often decreases with tensing
Intra-abdominal tumor: mass becomes less palpable with abdominal contraction

abdominal-wall-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

abnormal-uterine-bleeding.name: Abnormal uterine bleeding
abnormal-uterine-bleeding.scope: Adenomyosis, leiomyomas, endometrial polyps, ovulatory dysfunction, PALM-COEIN classification, endometrial biopsy
abnormal-uterine-bleeding.core: Abnormal uterine bleeding requires pregnancy exclusion, hemodynamic assessment and evaluation for structural disease or unopposed endometrial estrogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Perimenopause, PCOS, obesity, anticoagulants; lifelong heavy bleeding suggests inherited coagulopathy
Adenomyosis often multiparous; fibroids common during reproductive years

rows.label: Clues
items: Bleeding affecting quality of life, prolonged/heavy menses, intermenstrual or irregular bleeding
Tachycardia, orthostasis or syncope → clinically important blood loss
Postmenopausal bleeding requires malignancy evaluation even with a single episode

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PALM: Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy/hyperplasia → structural causes
COEIN: Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, Not otherwise classified
Anovulation → absent cyclic progesterone, unopposed proliferation and unstable shedding
Combined OCPs → uniform estrogen/progestin exposure **synchronizes endometrium**, preventing irregular shedding

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test and CBC** first; pelvic examination localizes uterine versus cervical/vaginal bleeding
**Transvaginal ultrasound** evaluates structural lesions; saline sonohysterography/hysteroscopy for intracavitary disease
★ **Endometrial biopsy ≥45 years**; younger with persistent bleeding, unopposed estrogen or failed treatment
Postmenopausal bleeding: endometrial thickness >4 mm → sampling; persistent bleeding → biopsy regardless of thickness
TSH for suspected endocrine disease; coagulation/vWF testing for suggestive bleeding history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → IV access, blood resuscitation, urgent gynecology; tamponade or operative control if needed
Stable → high-dose combined OCP, progestin, tranexamic acid; no estrogen if prior VTE, hypertension, smoker >35
★ Long-term → **levonorgestrel IUD**, OCP/progestin; family complete, normal cavity → **ablation**; copper worsens
Fibroids: asymptomatic → **observation, any size**; symptomatic → myomectomy/embolization; hysterectomy if childbearing done
Polyp → hysteroscopic removal; adenomyosis refractory to hormones → hysterectomy

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency anemia; chronic anovulation → endometrial hyperplasia/cancer; structural lesions can impair fertility

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular progestin exposure for chronic anovulation; replace iron and address metabolic drivers

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregnancy complication: positive hCG; exclude ectopic pregnancy
Cervicitis: friable cervix and postcoital bleeding

table.title: Cause clues
rows: Firm irregular enlarged uterus; pressure symptoms
Labor-like pain, dilated os, beefy prolapsing tissue
Tender uterus; biopsy **plasma cells**, not neutrophils

acetaminophen-toxicity.name: Acetaminophen toxicity
acetaminophen-toxicity.scope: Rumack-Matthew nomogram, 4-hour post-ingestion level, toxic metabolite NAPQI, N-acetylcysteine indications and timing, acute liver failure
acetaminophen-toxicity.core: Potentially toxic acetaminophen ingestion can be asymptomatic initially; time-specific concentration and hepatic injury determine immediate N-acetylcysteine treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Intentional overdose, repeated excessive dosing, unrecognized combination cold/pain products
Malnutrition and chronic heavy alcohol use increase vulnerability, especially with repeated supratherapeutic use
Extended-release products and opioid/anticholinergic co-ingestion may delay absorption

rows.label: Clues
items: First day: nausea/vomiting or no symptoms; next 1–3 days: RUQ pain, rising AST/ALT
★ **Coagulopathy, hypoglycemia, encephalopathy**, acidosis → severe hepatic failure
Early normal transaminases and clinical improvement do not establish safety

rows.label: Pathophys
items: CYP metabolism produces NAPQI; glutathione depletion → centrilobular hepatocyte necrosis
N-acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione and benefits established liver failure beyond toxin clearance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Known acute ingestion → **acetaminophen concentration at ≥4 hours**; earlier result cannot risk-stratify
★ Plot **Rumack–Matthew nomogram**, 4–24 h; treatment line starts 150 µg/mL at 4 h
Unknown timing/repeated supratherapeutic use → no nomogram; obtain concentration, AST/ALT, INR, glucose, creatinine
Delayed absorption and initial detectable subthreshold level → repeat concentration after 4–6 h
Assess co-ingestions/pregnancy; intentional ingestion → psychiatric safety evaluation after stabilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ At/above treatment line → **N-acetylcysteine**, ideally within 8 h; benefit persists when delayed
Likely substantial ingestion and result delayed beyond 8 h → start antidote while awaiting testing
Unknown time: >10 µg/mL or liver injury; repeated excess: ≥20 µg/mL or abnormal aminotransferases → treat
Recent acute overdose, protected airway → activated charcoal, usually within 4 h; toxicology consultation
Continue antidote until clearance and hepatic/coagulation recovery criteria met; acute liver failure → transplant center

rows.label: Complications
items: Fulminant hepatic failure, AKI, cerebral edema, hypoglycemia, death
IV antidote → non-IgE-mediated infusion reaction; pause/treat reaction, then resume when needed

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Count acetaminophen across all products**, avoid duplicate dosing, secure storage
Assess suicide risk and arrange mental-health care after deliberate ingestion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic hepatitis: preceding profound hypotension
Viral hepatitis: exposure/serology without toxic ingestion pattern

acute-bronchitis.name: Acute bronchitis
acute-bronchitis.scope: Viral etiology (influenza, parainfluenza, RSV), persistent postviral cough, absence of pneumonia findings, clinical diagnosis, symptomatic management (NSAIDs, bronchodilators), antibiotic stewardship
acute-bronchitis.core: Acute cough after an upper respiratory illness, with no evidence of pneumonia; usually viral and self-limited.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Influenza, parainfluenza, RSV and other respiratory viruses; close contact during respiratory outbreaks
Smoking and inhaled irritants worsen cough and delay recovery

rows.label: Clues
items: Cough with or without sputum, chest soreness, scattered rhonchi clearing after cough; transient wheezing
Symptoms commonly last 2–3 weeks; postinfectious cough can persist 3–8 weeks
★ **Purulent sputum alone** does not establish bacterial infection
Hypoxemia, focal crackles, sustained fever, tachypnea, hemoptysis → reassess diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transient bronchial inflammation, mucus production, and airway hyperresponsiveness after infection
Cough can outlast active viral replication; prolonged symptoms alone do not imply antibiotic benefit

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; routine sputum cultures and chest radiography unnecessary with reassuring vitals and examination
Chest x-ray if focal consolidation, temperature ≥38 °C, HR ≥100/min, or RR ≥24/min
Lower imaging threshold in frail older or immunocompromised adults; pneumonia may lack classic fever
Influenza/COVID testing if result changes antivirals or isolation; paroxysms/exposure → pertussis PCR

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **No antibiotics** for uncomplicated disease regardless of cough duration
Hydration, acetaminophen or ibuprofen for discomfort; dextromethorphan may offer limited cough relief
★ **Albuterol only with wheezing/airflow obstruction**; systemic steroids not routine
High-risk suspected influenza → oseltamivir; suspected pertussis → azithromycin to limit transmission

rows.label: Complications
items: Sleep disruption, chest wall strain, transient bronchospasm; persistent cough requires review for another cause
Unnecessary antibiotics → C. difficile, adverse reactions, antimicrobial resistance

rows.label: Prevention
items: Respiratory hygiene, smoking cessation, influenza/COVID vaccination; set expectations for cough duration
Return for worsening dyspnea, recurrent fever, dehydration, or new focal symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pneumonia: infiltrate and systemic illness or focal consolidation
Asthma: recurrent episodic cough/wheeze, reversible obstruction
Pertussis: prolonged paroxysms, posttussive emesis, exposure history

acute-coronary-syndromes.name: Acute coronary syndromes
acute-coronary-syndromes.scope: Unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI, cardiac biomarkers, risk stratification (HEART/TIMI), antiplatelet and anticoagulation, reperfusion
acute-coronary-syndromes.core: Acute myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque disruption: distinguish occlusive infarction needing immediate reperfusion from non-ST-elevation syndromes needing risk-guided invasive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, age, premature family CAD
Cocaine/stimulants, anemia, tachyarrhythmia may provoke ischemia; distinguish supply-demand injury from plaque rupture

rows.label: Clues
items: Pressure with arm/jaw radiation, diaphoresis, nausea; older adults/diabetes may have dyspnea or epigastric pain alone
Inferior MI with hypotension, clear lungs, raised JVP → suspect RV infarction
★ New murmur, pulmonary edema, shock after MI → **mechanical complication**, urgent echo
Unexplained crash/syncope + ischemic ECG → primary MI; troponin over trauma imaging

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet activation and thrombin-mediated clot reduce coronary perfusion; necrosis releases troponin
Type 2 MI: oxygen mismatch without acute atherothrombosis; treat precipitating cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG within 10 minutes**, repeat if nondiagnostic; serial high-sensitivity troponin using validated pathway
Posterior suspicion → V7–V9; inferior MI → right-sided leads; new LBBB alone insufficient for STEMI
★ **Do not wait for troponin before STEMI reperfusion**; bedside echo if diagnosis/complications uncertain
HEART ≤3 + negative serial troponins → low risk; TIMI/GRACE stratifies NSTE-ACS
STE: **V1–V6 → LAD**; **II, III, aVF + bradycardia → RCA**; I, aVL → circumflex

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Chewed aspirin**, P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulant such as heparin, high-intensity atorvastatin; oxygen only if hypoxemic
Nitroglycerin (**venodilation** → ↓preload) for pain unless hypotension, RV infarction, recent PDE5 inhibitor; avoid NSAIDs
★ STEMI → **primary PCI** within 90 minutes at PCI center, ≤120 minutes including transfer
IF PCI delay >120 minutes, symptoms <12 hours, no contraindication → fibrinolysis promptly, then transfer

rows.label: Complications
items: VT/VF, AV block, HF, cardiogenic shock; free-wall rupture
Later aneurysm/thrombus, embolism, Dressler syndrome; antithrombotics → bleeding
Post-MI murmur: **papillary rupture** → apical, no O₂ step-up; **septal rupture** → left sternal, RA→RV step-up

rows.label: Prevention
items: DAPT usually 12 months after ACS unless bleeding risk changes plan; cardiac rehabilitation, smoking cessation
ACE inhibitor/ARB for LV dysfunction; beta-blocker when stable, avoid in shock or acute decompensation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic dissection: abrupt tearing pain/pulse deficit; anticoagulation or lysis dangerous
Pericarditis: positional pleuritic pain, diffuse changes
PE: hypoxemia, thrombotic risk, RV strain

table.title: Syndrome branches
rows: Urgent catheterization if unstable; otherwise risk-guided angiography
Regional ST elevation or occlusion equivalent
Prior intracranial hemorrhage, active bleeding, suspected dissection
Stress or perfusion testing within 72 hours

adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.name: Adolescent confidentiality and care
adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.scope: Confidentiality principles, exceptions to parental notification, parental requests for drug testing, encouraging family involvement
adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.core: Provide adolescents private, developmentally appropriate care; explain confidentiality and its safety limits before sensitive questions.

rows.label: Principle
items: Confidentiality supports honest disclosure; consent authority and parental access vary by jurisdiction
Assent: involve the adolescent even when guardian permission remains necessary
Contraception: minors generally consent confidentially; no parental notice or pelvic exam required

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Interview alone** for sexual health, substance use, mood, violence, and safety
★ Explain permitted confidential services; protect portals, billing, and result notifications
Encourage trusted-adult involvement; never require disclosure for legally confidential services

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ Parental request for **drug testing** → discuss concern, interview teen; avoid covert testing
Do not promise absolute secrecy or automatically send sensitive findings to parents
Do not breach for experimental substance use without impairment → counsel, schedule **follow-up visit**

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Imminent danger, suspected **abuse/neglect/exploitation** → protective disclosure and reporting
Emergency treatment when delay risks serious harm; involve guardians when feasible
Emancipated minors generally self-consent; pregnancy alone does not universally confer emancipation

rows.label: Traps
items: Minor consent varies: STI, contraception, pregnancy, mental health, substance; **elective surgery** → parents
Mandatory reporting thresholds for consensual sexual activity depend on ages and local law
Disclose minimum necessary information; explain safety-driven disclosure to adolescent whenever feasible

adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics principles; jurisdiction-specific consent/reporting law must be verified locally.

adolescent-preventive-care.name: Adolescent preventive care
adolescent-preventive-care.scope: Leading causes of death, injury prevention, HEADSS psychosocial screening, adolescent screening tests
adolescent-preventive-care.core: Private, developmentally appropriate preventive visits identify injury risk, mental illness, substance use, sexual health needs, and barriers to healthy development.

rows.label: Who
items: All adolescents annually; explain confidentiality and safety exceptions, with some time alone
Leading death cause: **unintentional injury**, then suicide, homicide; risk varies by age and population

rows.label: Start/stop
items: HEADSS: Home, Education, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, Suicide/depression; include strengths and safety
★ Annual **depression and suicide-risk screening from 12**; assess younger patients when concerned
HIV once during adolescence, repeat with ongoing risk; lipids once at 17–21 years

rows.label: Test
items: ★ BP, BMI, development; **chlamydia/gonorrhea annually** for sexually active females <25
Exposure-site STI testing for MSM; syphilis/TB/anemia testing by risk
Assess sleep, nutrition, eating disorders, substances/vaping, violence, school, sexual coercion

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Positive suicide screen → **brief safety assessment**, urgent evaluation for imminent risk
Post-menarche → pregnancy/STI prevention, contraception; treat STIs; substance-use counseling; accessible follow-up
Counsel seat belts, helmets, no impaired/distracted driving; secure firearms unloaded and locked

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No routine Pap before 21**, even with sexual activity; STI screening uses separate tests
Depression screening alone misses some suicide risk; ask directly about thoughts and plans
Early post-menarche: irregular cycles normal, no hormone testing; update HPV, MenACWY, Tdap

adrenal-insufficiency.name: Adrenal insufficiency
adrenal-insufficiency.scope: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease), secondary adrenal insufficiency, cosyntropin stimulation test, morning serum cortisol, hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone replacement, adrenal crisis
adrenal-insufficiency.core: Weight loss, fatigue, orthostasis, and hyponatremia, or unexplained pressor-resistant shock after illness or interruption of glucocorticoids.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Primary: autoimmune destruction, TB, bilateral hemorrhage, metastases; associated autoimmune thyroid disease
★ Secondary: **prolonged glucocorticoids**, pituitary disease/surgery/apoplexy; abrupt withdrawal risks crisis
Crisis triggers: infection, trauma, surgery, missed replacement, vomiting

rows.label: Clues
items: Anorexia, abdominal pain, nausea, weakness; hypoglycemia, eosinophilia
Crisis: fever, confusion, severe volume depletion; symptoms may worsen rapidly during intercurrent illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cortisol deficiency reduces vascular catecholamine response and increases ADH
Primary gland failure removes mineralocorticoids; secondary disease retains renin–angiotensin-driven aldosterone

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **8 AM cortisol + ACTH**; very low cortisol supports, clearly high values argue against insufficiency
★ Equivocal basal cortisol → **cosyntropin (ACTH) stimulation**; inadequate assay-specific peak confirms impaired reserve
Traditional stimulated cutoff ≈18 µg/dL; newer assays may use ≈14–15; interpret laboratory standard
Primary → 21-hydroxylase antibodies, selected adrenal CT; secondary → pituitary evaluation/MRI
Recent pituitary injury may initially show normal cosyntropin response; clinical suspicion still matters

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crisis → draw blood if feasible, **IV hydrocortisone + isotonic saline**, dextrose for hypoglycemia
Do not wait for confirmatory results; treat precipitant and correct electrolytes carefully
Coexisting hypothyroidism → glucocorticoid replacement before levothyroxine to avoid decompensation

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated crisis → arrhythmia, circulatory collapse, death; chronic undertreatment → impaired function
Excess replacement → osteoporosis, diabetes, Cushingoid features

rows.label: Prevention
items: Stress-dose plan, emergency injectable hydrocortisone, medical alert ID; taper prolonged systemic steroids
Vomiting prevents absorption → parenteral replacement and urgent evaluation; teach sick-day plans to caregivers

rows.label: Mimics
items: SIADH: euvolemia, normal potassium and cortisol reserve
Sepsis: infection may coexist and trigger crisis
Hypothyroidism: bradycardia, cold intolerance, weight gain

table.title: Primary versus secondary
rows: Low/inappropriately normal ACTH; potassium usually normal

adrenal-insufficiency.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine teaching; cortisol cutoffs are assay dependent.

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all 19–59; ≥60 with risk/request; health worker anti-HBs negative post-series → revaccinate
**HIV any CD4**, liver disease/alcohol, COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal <50; liver → HepA/HepB
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Anti-HBs/anti-HAV/VZV IgG positive → immune, skip; otherwise **do not delay vaccination** for serology
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza**: severe immunosuppression, pregnancy (nonimmune → postpartum)
PCV15 → PPSV23: ≥8 weeks immunocompromised; older exams: PPSV23 alone; mild illness/antibiotics: no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern; inactivated influenza cannot cause flu, coincidental virus; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

advance-directives-and-surrogates.name: Advance directives and surrogate decisions
advance-directives-and-surrogates.scope: Living will, DNR/DNI orders, health care proxy, substituted judgment, best interests, advance care planning
advance-directives-and-surrogates.core: Follow the capable patient's current wishes; when capacity is absent, use valid directives and authorized surrogate judgment.

rows.label: Principle
items: Autonomy persists after incapacity through documented preferences and legally authorized decision-makers
Substituted judgment: patient's known values; best interests: benefits/burdens when preferences unknown

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Confirm capacity, directive validity, clinical applicability, and designated **health care proxy**
★ Apply the patient's instructions over conflicting surrogate preferences
Discuss goals, code status, surrogate early; terminal sole caregiver → plan **child guardianship**

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ **DNR limits CPR**; do not automatically withhold antibiotics, analgesia, nutrition, or other treatment
Dementia diagnosis, mild test errors, or disagreement ≠ incapacity; capacity is decision-specific
★ **Surrogate cannot compel contraindicated treatment** → withhold it; ethics consult unnecessary

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Capable patient may revise prior instructions; current informed choices control
No directive/proxy → adult next of kin; none eligible (minor relative) → **court guardian**
Clear directive/reported wishes/proxy–team agreement → no consult; unresolved conflict → ethics, court

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **DNI and DNR differ**; clarify acceptable ventilation and perioperative plans
Proxy needs no terminal illness; dementia tube-feeding request → review lack of benefit, harms
Surrogate conveys patient's known wishes, not own beliefs; missing paperwork doesn't block them

table.title: Documents and authority
rows: Durable health care power of attorney
Current medical order limiting specified intervention
Portable treatment orders for serious illness

advance-directives-and-surrogates.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics framework; document validity and surrogate hierarchy depend on jurisdiction.

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

table.title: Primary amenorrhea: high FSH or absent uterus → karyotype

amputation-and-prosthetics.name: Amputation and prosthetics
amputation-and-prosthetics.scope: Transtibial and transfemoral amputation, residual limb pain, bony prominence and osteophyte, phantom limb pain, prosthetic fitting and revision
amputation-and-prosthetics.core: Limb loss requiring level-appropriate prosthetic rehabilitation; post-amputation pain stems from residual limb pathology, poor socket fit, or phantom sensation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: **Peripheral arterial disease + diabetes** (most common); trauma, malignancy, severe infection
Residual limb volume fluctuations, improper prosthetic alignment, inadequate bone beveling

rows.label: Clues
items: Residual limb edema, skin breakdown, or focal pain worsening with weight-bearing
★ **Transtibial** preserves knee → lower energy cost and better gait than **transfemoral**
Red flags: purulence, spreading erythema, fever → deep infection or osteomyelitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Phantom pain: **central cortical reorganization** and deafferentation hypersensitivity after nerve transection
Heterotopic ossification: periosteal irritation at transected bone end causes focal mechanical pain

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Inspect residual limb + prosthetic socket** first for erythema, callus, or focal tenderness
★ **Plain X-ray** of residual limb to detect **bony prominence, osteophyte**, or osteomyelitis
MRI or ESR/CRP if deep abscess, neuroma, or osteomyelitis is suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Nonoperative prosthetic fitting/alignment** first for mechanical pain without infection
Pre-prosthetic rehab: **compressive shrinker** to shape stump and prevent flexion contractures
★ **Operative stump revision** (beveling/excision) if structural pain fails socket modification
Infection/ischemia → IV antibiotics, debridement, or revision to higher amputation level

rows.label: Complications
items: **Joint flexion contractures** (knee in transtibial, hip in transfemoral), skin ulceration, falls
Wound dehiscence, osteomyelitis, chronic neuropathic pain, depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Daily stump and liner hygiene; prone positioning and stretching to prevent **flexion contractures**
Regular prosthetist follow-up as residual limb matures and shrinks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Phantom limb sensation: non-painful awareness of missing limb; reassure without drugs
Cellulitis/osteomyelitis: warmth, fever, purulence rather than isolated pressure erythema
Lumbar radiculopathy: dermatomal pain from back with negative local stump exam

amputation-and-prosthetics.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic/PM&R teaching.

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.scope: Upper and lower motor neuron signs, bulbar symptoms, preserved sensation, EMG/NCS findings, noninvasive positive pressure ventilation, riluzole, edaravone, end-of-life planning
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.core: Progressive weakness with upper and lower motor neuron signs in multiple regions, usually with preserved sensation and sphincter function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Middle/older adulthood, male sex; mostly sporadic, minority familial
Family history of motor neuron disease or frontotemporal dementia supports inherited susceptibility

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Atrophy, fasciculations + hyperreflexia/spasticity** within affected regions; asymmetric limb onset common
Bulbar disease: dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue wasting; pseudobulbar affect may accompany corticobulbar dysfunction
Orthopnea, morning headache, weak cough → ventilatory weakness; inward abdominal motion on inspiration → **diaphragmatic paralysis**
Ocular movement and sensation usually spared; some patients develop executive or behavioral impairment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Degeneration of corticospinal neurons and anterior horn/bulbar motor neurons; denervation spreads progressively

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical progression + EMG/NCS**: widespread **fibrillation potentials**, sharp waves, chronic denervation; sensory conduction normal
MRI brain/spine to exclude structural mimics; targeted B12, thyroid, CK, and other studies
Assess FVC, inspiratory strength, nocturnal gas exchange, swallow function, nutrition; no single definitive blood test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Riluzole** modestly prolongs survival; edaravone may slow functional decline in selected patients
★ **Noninvasive ventilation** for symptomatic respiratory weakness improves comfort and survival
Swallow/nutrition support; discuss gastrostomy before severe respiratory decline; cough-assist and secretion management
Baclofen for spasticity, communication devices, physical/occupational support; multidisciplinary specialty care
Early shared planning for ventilation, feeding, advance directives, hospice; discuss choices before communication declines

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure is usual terminal event; aspiration, malnutrition, falls, immobility
Depression, caregiver burden; frontotemporal impairment may affect decision-making capacity

rows.label: Prevention
items: No primary prevention; aspiration/fall precautions, vaccination, nutritional support, respiratory surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical myelopathy: sensory level, sphincter changes, compressive MRI lesion
Myasthenia gravis: fatigable ocular weakness, no UMN signs
Multifocal motor neuropathy: conduction block, IVIG response

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.evidence: Not checked online; established ALS diagnosis and supportive-treatment teaching.

anaphylaxis.name: Anaphylaxis
anaphylaxis.scope: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, biphasic reactions, epinephrine autoinjector, emergency airway management
anaphylaxis.core: Rapid multisystem reaction after exposure—or isolated hypotension or airway compromise after a known allergen—requires epinephrine immediately.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Foods, insect venom, antibiotics, latex; exercise can amplify food-triggered reactions
Asthma, prior severe reaction, mast-cell disorders; beta-blockers can complicate treatment

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Urticaria/angioedema + wheeze, stridor, hypotension, or severe GI symptoms**
Skin findings may be absent; hoarseness and tongue swelling predict airway danger
Biphasic recurrence after apparent resolution, especially after severe or undertreated episodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mast-cell/basophil mediators → vasodilation, capillary leak, bronchoconstriction; often IgE-mediated
Epinephrine: α1 reverses vasodilation/edema, β2 reverses bronchoconstriction; albuterol alone misses edema and shock

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; never wait for tryptase or laboratory confirmation
Acute and baseline serum tryptase can support uncertain cases; normal results do not exclude anaphylaxis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IM epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg**, adult 0.3–0.5 mg, lateral thigh; repeat every 5–15 minutes
Supine with legs elevated unless respiratory distress; oxygen, early intubation for progressive obstruction
Profound shock or refractory hypotension → titrated IV epinephrine plus **isotonic boluses**; beta-blocker use → glucagon
Albuterol for residual bronchospasm; antihistamines relieve itching only; steroids do not reliably prevent biphasic reactions
★ Monitor until resolved; **longer observation/admission** after hypotension, repeated epinephrine, or severe asthma

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxia, distributive shock, arrhythmia, hypoxic brain injury
Undiluted IV epinephrine bolus errors → ischemia and dangerous dysrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prescribe **epinephrine autoinjector**, demonstrate technique, provide written action plan and allergy referral
Extra device for repeat-dose risk; avoidance, medical alert ID; venom immunotherapy after qualifying sting allergy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal episode: bradycardia, pallor, rapid improvement supine
Bradykinin angioedema: no itching/hives; ACE inhibitor or hereditary disease → airway, icatibant/C1 inhibitor

angioedema.name: Angioedema
angioedema.scope: Hereditary angioedema (C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency, C4 level), ACE inhibitor-induced, mast cell-mediated vs bradykinin-mediated, acute airway compromise, C1-INH concentrate, icatibant
angioedema.core: Deep, transient swelling of lips, tongue, airway, or bowel; distinguishing histamine from bradykinin determines which drugs will work.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Allergens, NSAIDs, insect stings → mast cell activation
Hereditary attacks: autosomal dominant history, trauma, dental procedures, estrogen exposure
ACE inhibitors: attacks possible even after years of uneventful use

rows.label: Clues
items: Nonpitting, asymmetric edema; gastrointestinal attacks may cause severe colicky pain, vomiting
★ Hoarseness, stridor, drooling, rapidly progressive tongue swelling → **airway emergency**
Recurrent episodes beginning in childhood support hereditary disease; late onset suggests acquired deficiency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Histamine increases vascular permeability through mast cell mediator release
C1-INH deficiency/dysfunction or impaired bradykinin breakdown → kallikrein-mediated vascular leakage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Recurrent nonurticarial attacks → **C4 plus C1-INH level and function**; repeat abnormal results
Low C1-INH quantity → type I; normal/high quantity with low function → type II
Normal C4 does not fully exclude HAE; C1q low in acquired, usually normal in hereditary disease
ACE inhibitor-related disease: clinical diagnosis; complement usually normal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Secure threatened airway early with expert intubation; prepare surgical airway
Uncertain mechanism with possible anaphylaxis → IM epinephrine immediately; do not await complement testing
★ ACE inhibitor-related: stop drug permanently; airway/supportive care; targeted drug evidence inconsistent
HAE attack: give available on-demand drug early; plasma if specific agents unavailable

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxiation, hypovolemia from bowel edema; unnecessary abdominal surgery after misdiagnosis
Recurrence may continue after ACE inhibitor discontinuation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ HAE: on-demand rescue supply; procedure prophylaxis with C1-INH; avoid ACE inhibitors and estrogen
Frequent HAE attacks → lanadelumab, berotralstat, or scheduled C1-INH; screen first-degree relatives

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: persistent warm, tender erythema with infection signs
Contact dermatitis: superficial pruritic, eczematous eruption rather than isolated deep swelling

table.title: Mediator guides treatment
rows: Epinephrine for anaphylaxis; H1 antihistamine adjunct

anorectal-disorders.name: Anorectal disorders
anorectal-disorders.scope: Anal fissure, internal and external hemorrhoids, anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, pruritus ani, topical vasodilators, fiber, sitz baths
anorectal-disorders.core: Anal pain, bleeding, swelling, or drainage requires inspection and focused examination; pain pattern distinguishes fissure, thrombosis, and infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constipation, straining, pregnancy, prolonged sitting; Crohn disease, diabetes, immunosuppression increase infection risk
Irritant soaps, moisture, fecal seepage contribute to pruritus ani

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pain out of proportion, fever, spreading erythema, crepitus** → evaluate necrotizing perineal infection urgently
Posterior midline fissure common; lateral/multiple fissures suggest Crohn disease, infection, or malignancy
Internal hemorrhoids lie above dentate line; prolapse may require manual reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fissure causes internal sphincter spasm and local ischemia; hemorrhoids represent enlarged vascular cushions
Cryptoglandular infection creates abscess; persistent epithelialized tract can become a fistula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Inspection first**, gentle DRE/anoscopy when tolerable; do not force painful fissure examination
Deep pain without visible lesion → CT/MRI for occult abscess; recurrent fistula → pelvic MRI
Rectal bleeding with anemia, weight loss, bowel change, or screening indication → colon evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Fiber, fluids, stool softening, **sitz baths**; fissure → topical anesthetic, nitroglycerin or diltiazem
Refractory chronic fissure → botulinum toxin or lateral internal sphincterotomy after continence-risk assessment
Internal hemorrhoids persisting despite conservative measures → rubber-band ligation; advanced prolapse → surgery
★ Abscess → **incision and drainage**; antibiotics added for cellulitis, systemic illness, or immunosuppression
Fistula → colorectal surgery; painful thrombosed external hemorrhoid within 72 hours → consider excision

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess recurrence, fistula, sepsis; sphincter injury → fecal incontinence
Chronic bleeding → iron deficiency; pruritus → excoriations and secondary infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid straining and prolonged toilet sitting; gentle cleansing, dry skin, barrier ointment for seepage

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anal cancer: persistent irregular ulcer/mass or large wart-like lesion, biopsy required
Proctitis: urgency, tenesmus, mucous discharge
Pinworm: nocturnal itch, especially children; tape test

table.title: Local patterns
rows: Tearing defecation pain; bright blood on paper
Recurrent purulent drainage from external opening

anorectal-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established colorectal teaching.

antepartum-bleeding.name: Antepartum bleeding
antepartum-bleeding.scope: Placenta previa, placental abruption, vasa previa, uterine rupture, transabdominal ultrasound before digital exam, Kleihauer-Betke test, emergent cesarean delivery
antepartum-bleeding.core: Bleeding in later pregnancy requires immediate maternal stabilization and fetal assessment, followed by placental localization before any digital cervical examination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previa: prior cesarean, multiparity; abruption: hypertension, cocaine, trauma, prior abruption
Vasa previa: velamentous cord, accessory placental lobe, IVF; rupture: uterine scar, obstructed labor

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock may exceed visible blood loss** with concealed abruption or internal hemorrhage
Assess uterine tone, pain, contractions, fetal tracing, membrane status; bleeding volume alone is unreliable

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maternal placental bleeding versus fetal vessel hemorrhage; vasa previa can rapidly exsanguinate fetus
Placental separation or uterine disruption compromises oxygen delivery independent of maternal external blood loss

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC, type/crossmatch, coagulation studies including fibrinogen; continuous fetal monitoring if viable
★ **Ultrasound before digital examination**; transabdominal first; transvaginal safely clarifies placenta–cervix relationship
Normal ultrasound does not exclude abruption; suspected rupture is a clinical emergency
Rh-negative bleeding/trauma → Kleihauer–Betke or flow cytometry quantifies fetomaternal hemorrhage for anti-D dosing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ ABCs, two large IVs, blood products when needed; **do not delay delivery for imaging if unstable**
Hemorrhage/fetal compromise → emergency cesarean; rupture → laparotomy, uterine repair or hysterectomy
Stable preterm previa → observation, pelvic rest, corticosteroids when eligible; planned cesarean before labor
Abruption: deliver if significant or compromised; vaginal birth possible when stable and imminent or fetal demise
Unsensitized Rh-negative patient → anti-D immunoglobulin; correct abruption-associated coagulopathy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, DIC, AKI, hysterectomy; fetal hypoxia, death, prematurity
Previa plus cesarean scar increases placenta accreta spectrum risk and operative hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP, avoid cocaine/tobacco; prenatal placental/cord localization and planned high-risk delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bloody show: small mucus-streaked bleeding with cervical change
Cervical lesion: contact bleeding, visible source on speculum examination

table.title: Critical distinctions
rows: Bleeding after rupture; sudden fetal bradycardia
Scarred uterus; sudden pain, lost station, fetal bradycardia

antepartum-bleeding.evidence: Not checked online; established obstetric hemorrhage teaching.

antiarrhythmics.name: Antiarrhythmic agents
antiarrhythmics.scope: Class I (sodium channel blockers), Class II (beta-blockers), Class III (amiodarone, sotalol), Class IV (calcium channel blockers), adenosine, adverse effects, toxicity
antiarrhythmics.core: Drug classes control cardiac rate/rhythm; select by stability, ventricular function, and risk of proarrhythmia.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Regular narrow-complex SVT after vagal maneuvers → rapid IV **adenosine**
Preexcited AF → procainamide or cardioversion; never AV-nodal blockers
AF rate → metoprolol/diltiazem; AF rhythm → selected IC/III; VT → amiodarone/lidocaine

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Adenosine transiently blocks AV-node conduction; does not terminate AF/flutter

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Amiodarone: **pulmonary fibrosis**, hypo/hyperthyroidism, hepatitis, photosensitivity, corneal deposits
Adenosine: flushing, chest pressure, brief asystole; avoid active bronchospasm

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ **Flecainide/propafenone** after MI or with significant structural heart disease
Verapamil/diltiazem in HFrEF; beta-blockers during cardiogenic shock or severe decompensation

rows.label: Interactions
items: Amiodarone increases warfarin and digoxin exposure; reduce doses and monitor
Beta-blocker + nondihydropyridine CCB → AV block; caffeine antagonizes adenosine

rows.label: Monitor
items: ECG, electrolytes, renal function; correct low K/Mg before QT-prolonging drugs
Amiodarone: baseline/periodic TSH, LFTs; baseline chest x-ray, evaluate new pulmonary symptoms

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Unstable tachycardia with pulse → **synchronized cardioversion**; pulseless VT/VF → defibrillation
Torsades → IV magnesium; recurrent pause-dependent episodes may need pacing

table.title: Classes
rows: QT/torsades; respectively cinchonism, lupus, anticholinergic effects

anticoagulants.name: Anticoagulants
anticoagulants.scope: Warfarin (CYP interactions, INR monitoring, reversal with vitamin K and PCC), heparin and LMWH (protamine reversal, HIT), direct oral anticoagulants (apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, reversal agents)
anticoagulants.core: Anticoagulants prevent clot extension and embolization; drug choice depends on indication, renal function, pregnancy, and bleeding risk.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ **DOACs**: most nonvalvular AF and VTE; warfarin: mechanical valves, rheumatic mitral stenosis
LMWH: pregnancy; UFH: rapid reversibility or severe renal impairment

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Warfarin blocks vitamin K recycling → ↓II, VII, IX, X and proteins C/S
UFH/LMWH enhance antithrombin; UFH inhibits IIa/Xa, LMWH predominantly Xa
Apixaban/rivaroxaban directly inhibit Xa; dabigatran directly inhibits thrombin

rows.label: Adverse
items: Bleeding with all; warfarin → early skin necrosis, fetal injury
★ **HIT**: platelet fall >50%, usually days 5–10; thrombosis more characteristic than bleeding
High INR + bowel obstruction, hemoglobin drop → **intramural small-bowel hematoma**

rows.label: Avoid
items: Suspected HIT → stop every heparin source; start argatroban or another nonheparin anticoagulant
Warfarin initiation during acute HIT; DOACs for mechanical valves or high-risk antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Interactions
items: Warfarin ↑: amiodarone, TMP-SMX/metronidazole, **fluoroquinolones**; ↓: rifampin, vitamin K-rich diet
DOAC exposure altered by strong P-glycoprotein/CYP3A modifiers; NSAIDs/antiplatelets increase bleeding

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Warfarin **INR**, usually 2–3; UFH aPTT/anti-Xa; LMWH/DOACs: renal function, CBC
No routine INR titration for DOACs; LMWH anti-Xa only selected situations

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Acute VTE warfarin → overlap parenteral anticoagulant ≥5 days and until therapeutic INR
Historical Xa antidote andexanet: US sales ended December 2025; use local PCC-based reversal protocols

antidepressants.name: Antidepressants
antidepressants.scope: SSRIs, SNRIs, bupropion, mirtazapine, tricyclic antidepressants (anticholinergic toxicity, urinary retention, arrhythmia), MAO inhibitors, adverse effects (serotonin syndrome)
antidepressants.core: SSRIs usually start depression treatment; choose alternatives by accompanying symptoms, adverse effects, and overdose risk.

rows.label: Use
items: SSRIs/SNRIs: depression, anxiety; duloxetine also neuropathic pain
Bupropion: smoking cessation; mirtazapine: poor appetite with insomnia
TCAs/MAOIs: resistant depression; TCAs also neuropathic pain

rows.label: Mechanism
items: SSRIs: serotonin reuptake blockade; SNRIs/TCAs: serotonin + norepinephrine reuptake blockade
Bupropion: norepinephrine/dopamine reuptake blockade; mirtazapine: α2 antagonism
MAOIs: reduced monoamine degradation

rows.label: Adverse
items: SSRIs: GI upset, SIADH, bleeding; SNRIs: ↑BP; mirtazapine: sedation/weight gain; bupropion: activating
★ SSRI **sexual dysfunction** → **lower dose** first; other SSRIs rarely help; bupropion minimal
TCAs: constipation, urinary retention, conduction toxicity; MAOIs: orthostatic hypotension

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ Bupropion lowers seizure threshold: **seizure or eating disorders**; CYP inhibitors raise levels
TCAs: urinary retention, glaucoma, conduction disease; anticholinergic delirium in older adults
TCA therapy with QTc/QRS prolongation → **stop TCA**, no waiting for levels

rows.label: Interactions
items: MAOI + tyramine/sympathomimetics → hypertensive crisis → **phentolamine** (α-blocker)
MAOI + SSRI/tramadol → serotonin syndrome; washout generally 14 days, after fluoxetine 5 weeks
Fluoxetine/paroxetine inhibit CYP2D6 → ↑TCA levels, toxicity

rows.label: Monitor
items: Mood, suicidality early in young adults; monitor adherence and functioning
Abrupt stop → **discontinuation**: flu-like aches, headache, dizziness, electric paresthesias, nausea, tremor
Response over 4–6 weeks; taper to stop, especially paroxetine and venlafaxine

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Serotonin syndrome**: clonus, fever/agitation → stop drugs, benzodiazepines; cyproheptadine
★ TCA overdose: Na⁺-channel blockade → **wide QRS**, arrhythmia, seizures → IV sodium bicarbonate
Bipolar depression: antidepressant monotherapy may provoke mania

antidepressants.evidence: Not checked online; established pharmacology and prescribing safety.

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.scope: Diagnosis, stepwise therapy, acute exacerbation, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
asthma.core: Variable episodes of wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from reversible expiratory airflow limitation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: **Family history of asthma/atopy**: strongest childhood risk; allergens, viral infections, smoke, occupational sensitizers
Exercise/cold air, aspirin-sensitive disease, nonselective beta-blockers; assess workplace symptom pattern

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal/early-morning symptoms; normal examination between attacks
★ **Silent chest, exhaustion, altered mentation, rising PaCO2** → impending respiratory failure
Acute attack: low peak flow, accessory-muscle use, difficulty speaking
Cough-variant: isolated chronic cough, worse with cold/exercise; normal examination and radiograph

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergen cross-links IgE on **mast cells** → histamine, leukotrienes → bronchoconstriction
Airway inflammation, smooth-muscle constriction, mucus → variable obstruction and hyperresponsiveness
Persistent uncontrolled inflammation → remodeling with incompletely reversible airflow limitation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Spirometry**: obstruction with bronchodilator FEV1 increase >12% and >200 mL in adults
Normal spirometry with suspicion → repeat during symptoms or methacholine challenge
Exercise challenge: postexercise FEV1 fall >10%; assess baseline control before isolated exercise diagnosis
PFT pattern: ↓FEV1, normal/↓FVC, normal/↑TLC from air trapping

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **repeated inhaled albuterol + ipratropium**, oxygen, early systemic glucocorticoids
Severe poor response → IV magnesium; deterioration → intubation; avoid sedatives and routine antibiotics
Exercise symptoms → preexercise albuterol or prescribed ICS-formoterol; persistent symptoms → improve controller
Check technique/adherence before stepping up; uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA → phenotype-directed biologic referral
Discharge: **PEF ≥70–80% predicted** (less wheeze is unreliable) + 5–7 day **oral prednisone** prevents relapse

rows.label: Complications
items: Status asthmaticus, pneumothorax, respiratory arrest
ICS → thrush/dysphonia; systemic steroids → osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Written action plan, trigger reduction, smoking cessation, spacer; rinse mouth after ICS
★ GINA: **no SABA-only treatment**, no LABA monotherapy; ICS with every reliever use
Older exam questions (NAEPP) may expect: symptoms ≤2 days/week, awakenings ≤2/month → **SABA alone**; more → daily ICS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inducible laryngeal obstruction: inspiratory stridor, inspiratory flow-loop flattening
COPD: persistent obstruction, smoking history
HF: edema, elevated JVP, cardiac findings
Deconditioning: obese/sedentary, exertional dyspnea; normal PFTs, no bronchodilator response

atherosclerotic-cardiovascular-disease.name: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
atherosclerotic-cardiovascular-disease.scope: Leading cause of death, risk factors (smoking, diabetes, hypertension), ASCVD risk calculation, primary prevention (statins, aspirin)
atherosclerotic-cardiovascular-disease.core: Plaque-driven coronary, cerebrovascular and peripheral arterial disease, a leading cause of death.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, high LDL, CKD, older age, premature family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional angina, transient focal neurologic deficits, or reproducible exertional calf pain
Often asymptomatic before first event

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Arterial LDL retention → inflammation and plaque; rupture or erosion → acute thrombosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ 2026 ACC/AHA: **PREVENT-ASCVD** for ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 mg/dL, no known ASCVD
Classic older questions: Pooled Cohort Equations; intermediate 7.5–<20%, high ≥20%
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium can refine risk

rows.label: Tx
items: Clinical ASCVD → high-intensity atorvastatin or rosuvastatin; antiplatelet therapy by vascular indication

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, ischemic stroke, limb ischemia, ischemic cardiomyopathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, exercise, Mediterranean-style diet, blood pressure and diabetes control
★ LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin without risk calculation
★ Age 40–75 with diabetes, CKD stage 3–4 or HIV → lipid-lowering therapy regardless of calculated risk
★ USPSTF aspirin: individualize ages 40–59 with ≥10% risk and low bleeding risk; avoid starting ≥60

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasospastic angina: rest episodes with transient ST elevation
Neurogenic claudication: relief with spinal flexion, preserved distal pulses

table.title: PREVENT 10-year risk and primary prevention
rows: Consider statin, especially with risk enhancers

atherosclerotic-cardiovascular-disease.evidence: Checked ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia guideline (2026) and USPSTF aspirin recommendation (2022).

bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.name: Bartholin gland cyst and abscess
bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.scope: Asymptomatic cyst, symptomatic cyst, acute Bartholin abscess, incision and drainage, Word catheter placement, marsupialization, excision for recurrent or older women
bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.core: Obstructed posterior vestibular gland causing a cyst or abscess; durable drainage prevents recurrence, and age determines the need for malignancy assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive age, prior duct obstruction, previous cyst/abscess; usually polymicrobial vaginal/enteric flora
STIs may coexist but most abscesses are not solely gonococcal or chlamydial

rows.label: Clues
items: Cyst: soft fluctuant, often painless; abscess: marked tenderness, erythema, difficulty sitting/walking
Gland location near 4 or 8 o'clock at vaginal opening; usually unilateral
Firm, fixed, irregular, recurrent, or postmenopausal lesion → malignancy concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Duct occlusion retains gland secretions; bacterial infection produces purulence
Drainage without an epithelialized outlet allows rapid closure and recurrence

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical vulvar examination**; assess cellulitis, systemic illness, pregnancy, immune status
GC/chlamydia NAAT when sexual risk or cervicitis; culture selected recurrent/severe infections
★ **Biopsy at age ≥40 or suspicious mass**; imaging unnecessary for typical superficial lesion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Management branches below; **Word catheter about 4 weeks** permits an epithelialized drainage tract
★ Avoid **incision alone or needle aspiration**: rapid closure causes recurrence
Antibiotics only for cellulitis, systemic infection, immunocompromise, or confirmed STI; uncomplicated drainage needs none
Persistent recurrence → gland excision after acute inflammation settles

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent abscess, surrounding cellulitis, rare sepsis; early catheter expulsion can compromise tract formation
Excision → bleeding, scarring, dyspareunia; older patients risk missed gland malignancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Complete catheter follow-up, hygiene without irritating products; condoms/STI treatment for exposure-related infection
No proven universal prevention of duct obstruction; return promptly for recurrent pain, fever, or mass

rows.label: Mimics
items: Skene duct cyst: periurethral/anterior location
Epidermal inclusion cyst: superficial skin nodule, possible punctum
Hidradenitis: recurrent multiple intertriginous nodules, sinus tracts

bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.evidence: Not checked online; established gynecologic office-procedure teaching.

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess
**Cracked, excoriated nipples** → main portal of entry for lactational mastitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: cystic lactational/postlactational mass, no inflammation, varies with feeds; fat–fluid level on imaging
Mastitis: focal tender erythema, fever, no fluctuance; abscess adds **fluctuance**; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → usually **papilloma**; exclude malignancy, persistent → surgical evaluation
Nonbloody discharge only on expression, normal exam → **physiologic**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma
Cyclic bilateral nodularity, no dominant mass → **reexamine after menses**, before imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Painful simple cyst → aspiration; nonbloody fluid + full collapse → benign; bloody fluid/residual mass → **biopsy**
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Breast pain, no mass, young, normal exam → **reassurance**; fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID
★ Mastitis → **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**, keep breastfeeding/pumping; abscess → add needle/incision drainage; MRSA → clindamycin
Tender lactating lump, no erythema/fever → **warm compresses**, keep nursing; persistent galactocele → aspiration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

table.title: Common benign findings
rows: Early postpartum; bilateral tense tender breasts, low fever

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

benign-skin-growths.name: Benign skin growths
benign-skin-growths.scope: Seborrheic keratosis, dermatofibroma, acrochordon, lipoma, epidermoid cyst
benign-skin-growths.core: Slow-growing, stable superficial lesions usually need reassurance; morphology guides recognition, while atypical change requires tissue diagnosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging → keratoses; friction, obesity, insulin resistance → skin tags
Minor trauma may precede dermatofibroma; blocked follicular openings favor epidermoid cysts
Lipomas often sporadic or familial; multiple lesions do not automatically imply malignancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Most lesions asymptomatic; irritation, snagging, cosmetic concern may prompt consultation
★ **Rapid growth, ulceration, spontaneous bleeding**, fixation, or new irregular pigment → reassess diagnosis
Deep, painful, enlarging soft-tissue mass, especially >5 cm → evaluate for sarcoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Benign keratinocyte, fibrous, adipose, or follicular proliferation; no inherent need for oncologic excision
Ruptured keratin cyst → sterile inflammation; erythema alone does not prove bacterial infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical lesions → **clinical examination**; compare with surrounding skin and prior photographs
Uncertain pigmented lesion → dermoscopy and biopsy; do not destroy before excluding melanoma
Suspicious deep mass → MRI and specialist-directed biopsy; ultrasound can establish superficial cystic character

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Reassurance** for confidently benign, untroublesome lesions; treatment chosen for symptoms or cosmetic goals
Irritated keratosis/tag → cryotherapy, snip, or shave removal; dermatofibroma usually observed
Symptomatic lipoma → excision; large/deep or suspicious masses need evaluation before office removal
★ Epidermoid cyst → **complete capsule excision** after inflammation subsides; fluctuant abscess → incision/drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: Local irritation, secondary infection, cyst rupture; removal → bleeding, scar, recurrence
Premature reassurance of atypical growth can delay cancer diagnosis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Melanoma: evolving asymmetric pigmentation, irregular border, color variation
Squamous cell carcinoma: indurated, scaly or ulcerated enlarging lesion
Liposarcoma: deep progressive mass rather than small soft mobile nodule

table.title: Morphologic recognition
rows: Firm papule; dimples with lateral compression

benign-skin-growths.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatologic morphology and evaluation principles.

bipolar-disorder.name: Bipolar disorder
bipolar-disorder.scope: Bipolar I (manic episode, DIG FAST), bipolar II (hypomania and major depression), cyclothymic disorder, acute mania pharmacotherapy (antipsychotics, lithium, valproate), maintenance therapy
bipolar-disorder.core: Distinct episodes of pathologically increased energy with elevated or irritable mood distinguish bipolar illness from ordinary mood variability.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong family history; typical onset adolescence/young adulthood
Sleep deprivation, antidepressants, stimulants, substances can precipitate episodes

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **DIG FAST**: distractibility, impulsivity, grandiosity, flight of ideas, activity, decreased sleep need, talkativeness
≥3 associated symptoms; ≥4 if mood only irritable
Mania: psychosis, marked impairment, risky spending/sex, or hospitalization; reduced sleep without fatigue

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial genetic vulnerability with dysregulated mood, reward and circadian systems

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical longitudinal history + collateral**; ask about prior elevated episodes before treating depression
Assess suicidality, pregnancy, substance use; TSH, metabolic panel, toxicology to exclude secondary causes
Hospitalization requirement can establish manic duration criterion even before one week
Major depression ≥2 weeks; hypomania causes no psychosis, marked impairment or hospitalization
Cyclothymia: symptoms ≥half the time; no symptom-free interval >2 months or full mood episodes

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute mania → **antipsychotic** (olanzapine/quetiapine); severe → add lithium/valproate; mixed/rapid cycling → **divalproex**
Unsafe, psychotic, severely agitated, or unable to care for self → hospitalization
Depression → quetiapine, lurasidone, lithium, lamotrigine; urgent/refractory or first-trimester psychotic mania → **ECT**
★ **Avoid antidepressant monotherapy**; lamotrigine does not treat acute mania
Maintenance: lithium, quetiapine, valproate or lamotrigine selected by episode pattern; lithium reduces suicide risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, substance misuse, financial/relationship loss; metabolic adverse effects of antipsychotics
Lithium: renal/thyroid toxicity; valproate/carbamazepine: teratogenicity, avoid in first trimester; lamotrigine: severe rash

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular sleep, psychoeducation, relapse-sign monitoring, maintenance adherence; avoid stimulants and substance misuse

rows.label: Mimics
items: ADHD: chronic baseline symptoms rather than distinct mood episodes
Borderline personality: brief reactive shifts linked to interpersonal stress
Medication/substance-induced mania: onset after antidepressant, stimulant, steroid → **stop culprit first**
Hyperthyroidism: heat intolerance, tremor, low TSH

table.title: Diagnostic branches
rows: Hypomania ≥4 days + major depression; never mania

breast-cancer-screening.name: Breast cancer screening
breast-cancer-screening.scope: USPSTF screening mammography recommendations, age-based intervals, high-risk screening (BRCA, prior chest radiation, breast MRI), clinical breast exam, diagnostic evaluation of abnormal screening
breast-cancer-screening.core: USPSTF recommends biennial mammography from ages 40–74 for average-risk women; symptoms require diagnostic evaluation regardless of screening schedule.

rows.label: Who
items: Average risk includes family history or dense breasts without a defined high-risk syndrome
★ BRCA pathogenic variant, young chest irradiation or lifetime risk **≥20–25%** → high-risk pathway

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Age ≥75: insufficient USPSTF evidence; individualize by health, life expectancy and preference
High risk: annual MRI plus mammography, typically around age 30; specialist-tailored earlier MRI
BRCA1/2: **bilateral mastectomy + salpingo-oophorectomy** = greatest risk reduction; tamoxifen weaker

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Digital mammography/tomosynthesis; **MRI supplements**, not replaces, high-risk mammography
Clinical breast examination and breast self-examination do not substitute for imaging

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ BI-RADS 0 → **diagnostic views/targeted ultrasound**; 4–5 → core needle biopsy
BI-RADS 3 → short-interval imaging, usually 6 months; 1–2 → routine interval
Palpable concerning mass with negative imaging → tissue assessment for clinical–radiologic discordance

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Older teaching: 50; **2024 USPSTF starts at 40**; other societies accept annual
Dense breasts alone: insufficient USPSTF evidence for routine supplemental ultrasound/MRI
Harms: false positives, biopsy, overdiagnosis; concerning mass needs evaluation despite normal mammogram

breast-neoplasia.name: Breast neoplasia
breast-neoplasia.scope: Ductal carcinoma in situ, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), metastatic disease (bone, visceral), surgical management, endocrine and chemotherapy
breast-neoplasia.core: A suspicious breast lesion requires core biopsy, assessment of invasion and ER/PR/HER2 status to guide local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, BRCA-related syndromes, close-relative family history (distant relative adds little), prior chest irradiation
**Combined estrogen-progestin therapy**, prolonged estrogen, postmenopausal obesity, alcohol; atypical proliferative lesions

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless hard irregular mass, skin/nipple retraction, unilateral bloody discharge or axillary node
★ Peau d’orange, diffuse erythema and edema → **inflammatory breast cancer**, even without discrete mass
Persistent unilateral eczematous nipple lesion → Paget disease; **full-thickness biopsy**, investigate underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Invasion through basement membrane enables lymphatic/hematogenous metastasis
ER/PR signaling and HER2 amplification create actionable tumor drivers; triple-negative tumors lack these targets

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diagnostic mammography + targeted ultrasound** → core biopsy of suspicious lesion; pregnancy → **ultrasound first**
Pathology: invasion, grade, **ER/PR/HER2**; assess regional nodes clinically and with targeted imaging
Clinically node-negative invasive disease, including microinvasion ≤1 mm → sentinel node biopsy during definitive surgery
Distant staging scans for advanced disease or suspicious symptoms; not every small asymptomatic cancer
Axillary node adenocarcinoma, normal mammogram → occult breast primary; breast MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early: lumpectomy + radiation or mastectomy; **positive margins → reexcision** before adjuvant therapy
ER-positive → tamoxifen or postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor; chemotherapy based on stage/biology
★ HER2-positive → **trastuzumab-based** treatment, monitor LVEF; triple-negative → chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab if higher-risk
Locally advanced → neoadjuvant treatment, then surgery/radiation; large residual + palpable nodes → **mastectomy + axillary dissection**
Bone metastases → **zoledronate/denosumab**; systemic treatment by receptors, chemotherapy for visceral crisis

rows.label: Complications
items: Metastases to bone (often **mixed lytic–blastic**), lung, liver, brain; surgery/radiation → lymphedema
Tamoxifen → VTE/endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors → bone loss; trastuzumab → cardiomyopathy
Prior cancer + severe hypercalcemia, lytic lesions → recurrence; thiazide/calcium supplements cause only mild elevation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Age/risk-based screening, genetic counseling for suggestive pedigree; selected high-risk patients → chemoprevention
BRCA-related very high risk → discuss risk-reducing surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mastitis: lactation-associated tenderness/fever, improves with antibiotics
Fat necrosis: trauma/surgery history; biopsy if discordant imaging

table.title: Histologic distinctions
rows: Bilateral risk marker; discohesive lobular cells
Surveillance/risk reduction if concordant; later cancer usually ductal

breast-neoplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established breast-oncology management principles.

carcinoid-syndrome.name: Carcinoid syndrome
carcinoid-syndrome.scope: Neuroendocrine tumors (midgut, bronchial), episodic cutaneous flushing, secretory diarrhea, tricuspid and pulmonary valvular disease, 24-hour urine 5-HIAA, octreotide therapy, surgical resection
carcinoid-syndrome.core: Episodic flushing and secretory diarrhea in a patient with a neuroendocrine tumor, often with liver metastases.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Midgut NET, especially ileal; bronchial NET with systemic venous drainage

rows.label: Clues
items: Watery stools persist during fasting; episodic wheezing
★ Right-sided valve disease: **tricuspid regurgitation** and pulmonic stenosis; edema, JVD
Left-sided valve disease possible with bronchial NET or right-to-left intracardiac shunt
Carcinoid crisis: abrupt hypotension or hypertension, bronchospasm and hemodynamic instability

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hepatic metabolism normally clears portal vasoactive products; hepatic metastases or systemic drainage bypass first pass
Serotonin drives diarrhea and endocardial fibrosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **24-hour urine 5-HIAA**; avoid serotonin-rich foods and interfering drugs before collection
CT/MRI and somatostatin receptor PET for localization and staging; tissue grading guides tumor therapy
NT-proBNP >260 pg/mL or cardiac signs → echocardiogram

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Octreotide** or lanreotide for hormonal symptoms and tumor control
Resect localized disease; selected metastatic cases → hepatic debulking or liver-directed therapy
Refractory diarrhea despite somatostatin analog → add telotristat
