Dopamine-blocking antipsychotics/metoclopramide cause secondary parkinsonism rather than idiopathic disease
MPTP (synthetic heroin contaminant) → rapid parkinsonism from nigral dopaminergic neuron destruction

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Resting pill-rolling tremor, cogwheel rigidity**, reduced arm swing, shuffling gait
Freezing, micrographia, hypophonia; pull test reveals impaired postural recovery, typically later
Constipation, anosmia, REM sleep behavior disorder, depression and autonomic symptoms can precede motor disease
Early severe falls, gaze palsy, marked autonomic failure or poor treatment response → atypical syndrome

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Substantia nigra dopaminergic neuron loss; α-synuclein Lewy bodies
Reduced striatal dopamine disrupts basal ganglia motor regulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; bradykinesia plus resting tremor and/or rigidity
Brain MRI for atypical findings; dopamine transporter imaging if uncertain degenerative versus nondegenerative tremor
Review medications; assess cognition, orthostatic BP, gait and swallowing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Function-limiting motor symptoms → **carbidopa/levodopa**, preferred initial dopaminergic treatment
Pramipexole/ropinirole for selected younger patients; avoid with hallucinations, impulse-control problems or age >70
Wearing-off → adjust levodopa schedule, add MAO-B/COMT inhibitor; dyskinesia → amantadine
★ Exercise, PT/speech/swallow rehab; refractory fluctuations/tremor/dyskinesias → **deep brain stimulation**, pallidotomy
Psychosis → reduce provoking drugs; pimavanserin or selected quetiapine/clozapine, avoid potent dopamine blockers

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration, dementia; medication → hallucinations, orthostasis, motor fluctuations/dyskinesias
Dopamine agonists → gambling/hypersexuality and sleep attacks; abrupt withdrawal → severe rigidity/hyperthermia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fall-proof home, medication adherence, aspiration-risk assessment; no established primary neuroprotective treatment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Essential tremor: action/postural tremor without decrementing bradykinesia
Drug-induced: blocker exposure, often symmetric; normal-pressure hydrocephalus: magnetic gait, urinary/cognitive symptoms

table.title: Atypical parkinsonism
rows: Severe orthostasis/urinary dysfunction, possible cerebellar signs
Dementia before or within 1 year of parkinsonism

patient-confidentiality.name: Patient confidentiality
patient-confidentiality.scope: HIPAA, exceptions to confidentiality, Tarasoff duty to protect, mandatory reporting vs law enforcement requests, substance use privacy, subpoena vs court order
patient-confidentiality.core: Protect identifiable health information unless authorized by the patient or a specific legal basis permits disclosure.

rows.label: Principle
items: HIPAA permits treatment, payment, and health care operations disclosures without authorization

rows.label: Do
items: Verify authority, document rationale, and disclose minimum necessary information when applicable

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ Police request alone → no chart release; confirm a specific lawful basis

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Report suspected child abuse and designated infections under state law
★ Tarasoff: serious threat → warn target, notify police, or hospitalize as state law requires

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Court order** → specified records only; civil subpoena alone generally insufficient
★ **Part 2 SUD records**: legal use against patient requires consent or order plus subpoena
Adult with capacity controls routine disclosures to family

patient-confidentiality.evidence: Checked HHS HIPAA Privacy Rule and 42 CFR Part 2 final rule (2024).

pediatric-abdominal-masses.name: Pediatric abdominal masses
pediatric-abdominal-masses.scope: Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma, WAGR, Beckwith-Wiedemann), neuroblastoma (adrenal medulla, crosses midline, catecholamines, N-myc), hydronephrosis, hepatoblastoma, ultrasound evaluation
pediatric-abdominal-masses.core: A child's abdominal mass: establish its organ of origin before biopsy; renal, sympathetic, hepatic, and obstructive lesions require different management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ Wilms: **WAGR**—aniridia, genitourinary anomalies, intellectual disability
Wilms: Beckwith-Wiedemann—macroglossia, omphalocele, hemihyperplasia
Hepatoblastoma: very low birth weight, Beckwith-Wiedemann, familial adenomatous polyposis
Hydronephrosis: congenital urinary obstruction or vesicoureteral reflux

rows.label: Clues
items: Often found incidentally during bathing; persistent enlargement, weight loss, pallor suggest malignancy
Neuroblastoma dissemination: periorbital ecchymoses, bone pain; opsoclonus-myoclonus possible
★ Weakness, gait change, bladder dysfunction → possible spinal cord compression

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Wilms: embryonal renal tumor; neuroblastoma: neural crest-derived adrenal medulla or sympathetic chain
Hepatoblastoma: embryonal hepatic malignancy; hydronephrosis: collecting-system dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Abdominal ultrasound** first → solid versus cystic and renal versus extrarenal origin
Solid lesion → contrast CT/MRI abdomen; chest imaging for malignant staging
Neuroblastoma: tissue diagnosis, MYCN testing, MIBG imaging, bone marrow assessment for staging
MYCN amplification → unfavorable prognosis; age and stage also determine neuroblastoma risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected Wilms: avoid repeated vigorous palpation and routine percutaneous biopsy; US approach usually nephrectomy first
Wilms: surgery + vincristine/dactinomycin-based chemotherapy; radiation for higher-risk disease
Neuroblastoma: low risk → observation/resection; high risk → chemotherapy, surgery, transplant, anti-GD2 immunotherapy
Hepatoblastoma: cisplatin-based chemotherapy + resection; unresectable liver-confined disease → transplant evaluation
Hydronephrosis: infected obstruction → urgent drainage; progressive functional loss → corrective surgery

rows.label: Complications
items: Tumor rupture/spillage worsens Wilms staging; bilateral disease threatens renal function
Hydronephrosis → infection, renal injury; neuroblastoma → marrow failure or cord compression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Syndrome-specific abdominal ultrasound surveillance for children predisposed to embryonal tumors

rows.label: Mimics
items: Constipation: fecal loading, improves after stool evacuation
Ovarian mass: pelvic/adnexal origin; torsion causes acute pain

pediatric-hip-disorders.name: Pediatric hip disorders
pediatric-hip-disorders.scope: Developmental dysplasia of the hip, Legg-Calve-Perthes disease, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, transient synovitis, pediatric limp workup
pediatric-hip-disorders.core: A child’s limp or knee pain may originate in the hip; age, weight-bearing ability, and hip rotation separate common developmental disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Breech presentation, female sex, family history → developmental hip dysplasia
Obesity and adolescence → slipped capital femoral epiphysis; atypically young/thin cases suggest endocrine disease
Recent viral illness → transient synovitis; Perthes often boys aged 4–8 years

rows.label: Clues
items: Infant asymmetric abduction or leg length; older child limp, groin/thigh/knee pain
★ **Fever, toxic appearance, refusal to bear weight**, painful restricted motion → septic arthritis concern
SCFE: obligate external rotation with flexion, limited internal rotation/abduction; Perthes: gradual painless/painful limp with limited internal rotation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysplasia: shallow acetabulum and unstable femoral head; Perthes: femoral-head avascular necrosis
SCFE: physeal failure displaces epiphysis relative to neck; synovitis: transient sterile joint inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Examine hip in unexplained knee pain**: gait, rotation, fever; limited rotation → **hip x-ray**, not knee MRI
DDH: Ortolani reduces dislocation; Barlow provokes instability; limited abduction more useful after early infancy
Risk-based DDH imaging → ultrasound around 6 weeks; radiograph after femoral ossification, usually ≥4–6 months
Suspected septic hip → CBC, ESR/CRP, cultures, ultrasound for effusion → urgent aspiration
Kocher features: fever >38.5°C, nonweight-bearing, WBC >12,000, ESR >40; support concern, never replace aspiration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected SCFE → **immediate nonweight-bearing**, orthopedic fixation; no forceful manipulation
★ Septic joint → **urgent drainage + IV antibiotics** after cultures when feasible
Transient synovitis → rest, NSAID, close reassessment; persistent/worsening symptoms require renewed evaluation
Perthes → orthopedic containment/ROM plan; DDH treatment depends on age and stability below

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated dysplasia → early osteoarthritis; SCFE → avascular necrosis/chondrolysis
Perthes → femoral-head deformity; missed septic arthritis → irreversible joint destruction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Newborn and infant hip examinations; avoid tight swaddling with extended adducted hips

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: focal bony tenderness, MRI marrow changes
Trauma: injury history and fracture imaging

table.title: Imaging and definitive branch
rows: Sclerosis, flattening, fragmentation; decreased bone-scan uptake

pediatric-hip-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric orthopedic assessment principles.

pericardial-disease.name: Pericardial disease
pericardial-disease.scope: Acute pericarditis, pericardial effusion, tamponade, constrictive pericarditis
pericardial-disease.core: Pericardial inflammation, fluid accumulation, or fibrosis produces distinct chest-pain and impaired-filling syndromes; hemodynamic effect depends on accumulation rate.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Viral/idiopathic, autoimmune disease, uremia, malignancy, TB, radiation, cardiac surgery
Early post-MI inflammation or delayed immune-mediated Dressler syndrome; trauma/anticoagulation can cause hemopericardium

rows.label: Clues
items: Pericarditis: sharp pleuritic positional pain, better leaning forward; friction rub may be transient
★ Tamponade: **hypotension, elevated JVP, muffled sounds**, pulsus paradoxus >10 mmHg; triad often incomplete
Constrictive disease: edema/ascites, Kussmaul sign, pericardial knock, prominent y descent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflamed surfaces cause pain; fluid or scar limits diastolic filling and stroke volume
Tamponade equalizes diastolic pressures; constriction exaggerates ventricular interdependence with respiration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pericarditis: ≥2 of **typical pain, rub, diffuse ST elevation/PR depression, new effusion**
Troponin elevation suggests myocardial involvement; CRP supports inflammation; echo assesses fluid and ventricular function
★ **Urgent bedside echo** for suspected tamponade: right-sided chamber collapse, plethoric IVC
Constrictive suspicion → echo, CT/MRI for thickening/calcification; catheterization if diagnosis remains uncertain

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tamponade → **urgent pericardiocentesis**; IV fluids bridge; avoid diuresis/positive-pressure ventilation
Purulent, traumatic, malignant, or recurrent effusion → surgical drainage/window; antibiotics for bacterial cause
Stable effusion → treat cause, serial echo; low voltage alone never determines drainage
High-risk features → admit: fever, large effusion, immunosuppression, anticoagulation, subacute onset, NSAID failure
Early post-cardiac-surgery tamponade → **urgent mediastinal re-exploration**

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent inflammation, arrhythmia/myocarditis, obstructive shock; procedural drainage → cardiac injury
Rapid decompression can rarely cause ventricular dysfunction; NSAIDs → GI/renal injury, colchicine → diarrhea

rows.label: Prevention
items: Colchicine course: first episode 3 months; recurrence ≥6 months; taper anti-inflammatory drugs after remission
Exercise restriction until clinical/inflammatory resolution; optimize dialysis for uremic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: STEMI: regional ST elevation with reciprocal changes; urgent coronary evaluation if uncertain
Restrictive cardiomyopathy: myocardial disease, less respiratory ventricular discordance
PE: thrombotic risk, acute RV strain

table.title: Nonemergency definitive management
rows: Ibuprofen + colchicine; aspirin preferred after MI
Selected low-dose glucocorticoid or IL-1 blockade

peripheral-artery-disease.name: Peripheral artery disease
peripheral-artery-disease.scope: Claudication, aortoiliac (Leriche) disease, critical and acute limb ischemia
peripheral-artery-disease.core: Atherosclerotic limb hypoperfusion ranges from exertional claudication to rest pain, tissue loss, or abrupt limb-threatening arterial occlusion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, age, CKD, hypertension, dyslipidemia; coronary/cerebrovascular atherosclerosis commonly coexists
AF, aneurysm, graft disease, hypercoagulability predispose acute occlusion

rows.label: Clues
items: Diminished pulses, cool shiny skin, hair loss, dependent rubor, distal nonhealing ulcers
★ **Pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia** → acute limb ischemia
Sensory/motor deficits signal threatened limb; do not await all six findings
Abrupt onset + AF, even with prior claudication → **embolus**, not in situ thrombosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fixed arterial narrowing limits exercise perfusion; progressive failure reduces resting tissue oxygenation
Acute embolus/thrombus prevents collateral compensation, rapidly injuring nerves and muscle
Subclavian stenosis proximal to vertebral origin → arm exercise reverses ipsilateral vertebral flow; brachiocephalic lesion: right arm + carotid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ABI ≤0.90** confirms PAD; 0.91–0.99 borderline; >1.40 suggests noncompressible arteries
Exertional symptoms with normal resting ABI → exercise ABI; noncompressible vessels → toe-brachial index
Duplex, CTA/MRA define anatomy when revascularization planned; acute ischemia: bedside Doppler, **arteriography with runoff**
Subclavian steal → **compare BP in both arms** (gap >15 mm Hg); confirm with duplex or **MR angiography**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic PAD: **clopidogrel or aspirin + high-intensity statin**, smoking cessation, structured exercise
Cilostazol improves claudication; contraindicated in any heart failure
Refractory disabling claudication → revascularization; chronic limb-threatening ischemia with distal target → **surgical bypass** before amputation
★ Acute ischemia → **IV unfractionated heparin, vascular consultation** without awaiting imaging; salvageable limb → urgent reperfusion
Low bleeding risk, symptomatic/postrevascularization → low-dose rivaroxaban + aspirin; no full anticoagulation solely for PAD

rows.label: Complications
items: Gangrene, infection, amputation; MI/stroke often dominate long-term mortality
Reperfusion → compartment syndrome, hyperkalemia, rhabdomyolysis; irreversible or nonfunctional limb (nonambulatory, contractures) → primary amputation
Popliteal aneurysm: pulsatile popliteal mass, distal emboli; large → **tibial nerve compression** (posterior knee/calf pain)

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Daily foot inspection**, protective footwear, diabetic foot care, BP/glucose control
Avoid thermal injury to insensate feet; antithrombotic plan after procedures based on bleeding risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Spinal stenosis: flexion relieves walking pain, pulses preserved
Venous ulcer: medial ankle, edema, pulses intact; neuropathy: sensory loss without ischemic pulse findings
Thoracic outlet syndrome: symptoms on arm abduction, no posterior-circulation ischemia

table.title: Clinical patterns
rows: Reproducible exercise pain relieved by rest
Buttock claudication, erectile dysfunction, weak femorals
Calf claudication; normal femoral, weak pedal pulses
Arm-exercise dizziness/syncope or claudication; weak ipsilateral pulse

peripheral-neuropathy.name: Peripheral neuropathy
peripheral-neuropathy.scope: Distal symmetric polyneuropathy, chemotherapy-induced (cisplatin, paclitaxel), HIV-associated neuropathy, alcohol-related, neuropathic pain pharmacotherapy (TCAs, gabapentinoids, SNRIs)
peripheral-neuropathy.core: Length-dependent injury produces symmetric distal sensory symptoms beginning in the feet and progressing proximally before the hands become involved.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Diabetes, alcohol use, CKD, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, HIV
Cisplatin/paclitaxel exposure; older neurotoxic ART such as stavudine; malnutrition

rows.label: Clues
items: Burning pain, allodynia or numbness; reduced vibration, ankle reflexes and distal sensation
★ **Asymmetry, rapid progression, motor predominance or marked autonomic findings** → urgent expanded evaluation
Small-fiber neuropathy: pain/temperature loss with initially preserved strength and nerve conduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Axonal dying-back affects longest fibers first; demyelinating neuropathy produces disproportionate conduction slowing

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Glucose/A1c, B12 with methylmalonic acid if borderline, SPEP with immunofixation**
CBC, metabolic panel, TSH; HIV testing according to exposure and clinical context
EMG/nerve conduction for atypical features, unclear diagnosis, or suspected demyelination
Normal studies do not exclude small-fiber disease; skin biopsy can confirm selected cases

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat cause: glycemic control, B12, alcohol cessation/nutrition, optimize ART; review neurotoxic drugs
★ Pain → **duloxetine, gabapentin/pregabalin, or TCA**; choose by comorbidity and adverse effects
Gabapentinoids: sedation/edema, renal dose adjustment; TCAs: anticholinergic effects, cardiac risk in older adults
★ Painful chemotherapy neuropathy → **duloxetine**; discuss dose reduction/substitution with oncology
Topical lidocaine/capsaicin for localized symptoms; avoid chronic opioids

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, painless ulcers, infection, Charcot arthropathy; orthostatic hypotension with autonomic involvement
Pain treatment reduces symptoms without restoring lost sensation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Daily foot inspection, protective footwear, monofilament assessment, fall prevention
Treat nutritional deficiencies; monitor symptoms during neurotoxic chemotherapy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Radiculopathy: dermatomal, often asymmetric pain and weakness
Myelopathy: hyperreflexia, sensory level, bowel/bladder dysfunction
Peripheral arterial disease: exertional pain, reduced pulses rather than sensory stocking loss
Charcot-Marie-Tooth: adolescent **pes cavus, hammer toes**, distal wasting, slowed conduction, family history

personality-disorders.name: Personality disorders
personality-disorders.scope: Cluster A (paranoid, schizoid, schizotypal), Cluster B (borderline, antisocial, histrionic, narcissistic), Cluster C (avoidant, dependent, OCPD), dialectical behavior therapy
personality-disorders.core: Enduring, inflexible patterns of cognition, affect, relationships, or impulse control cause impairment across settings beginning by adolescence or early adulthood.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Temperament, genetic susceptibility, early adversity and disrupted attachment; avoid attributing diagnosis to trauma alone
Traits must exceed cultural expectations; diagnose cautiously during acute illness or developmental transitions

rows.label: Clues
items: Cluster A: paranoid—distrust; schizoid—detachment; schizotypal—magical thinking, odd speech/perceptions, social discomfort
Cluster B: antisocial—violations of rights; histrionic—attention seeking; narcissistic—grandiosity/entitlement
Cluster C: avoidant—fears rejection/embarrassment, avoids new activities; dependent—clinging; OCPD—rigid perfectionism, control
★ Borderline: **splitting, unstable identity/relationships, self-harm**, abandonment fear, chronic emptiness, impulsivity

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maladaptive trait patterns impair emotion regulation and interpersonal functioning; no diagnostic biomarker
Impulsive aggression, violent suicide → **low CSF 5-HIAA** (serotonin metabolite)

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Longitudinal clinical assessment** across contexts; obtain collateral with consent
Exclude mood episodes, psychotic illness, substances, neurodevelopmental disorders and acquired brain disease
★ Antisocial diagnosis requires **age ≥18 plus conduct disorder before 15**
Borderline may cause brief stress-related paranoia/dissociation; sustained psychosis requires broader evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Borderline → **dialectical behavior therapy**; structured psychotherapy and consistent team boundaries
Trait-matched psychotherapy, e.g., avoidant → **CBT**, assertiveness training; clear expectations, empathic, nonpunitive tone
No medication treats personality disorder globally; target comorbid depression/anxiety or limited severe symptoms
Self-harm threats → assess intent, plan, access and safety; imminent risk → emergency psychiatric care
Avoid staff splitting through shared care plans; avoid reflexive long-term benzodiazepines in impulsive patients

rows.label: Complications
items: Self-injury/suicide, substance misuse, impaired work/relationships; antisocial traits → legal or violence consequences
Stigma and inconsistent treatment worsen engagement; therapeutic ruptures require careful repair

rows.label: Mimics
items: Autism: early developmental social-communication differences and restricted interests
Delusional disorder: fixed delusion rather than generalized suspicious personality style

personality-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

table.title: Common diagnostic confusions
rows: Reactive hours-long shifts vs sustained mood episodes
Odd beliefs vs persistent frank psychosis

pertussis.name: Pertussis
pertussis.scope: Bordetella pertussis, catarrhal, paroxysmal, and convalescent stages, posttussive emesis, inspiratory whoop, macrolide therapy, postexposure prophylaxis, Tdap vaccination
pertussis.core: Prolonged paroxysmal cough with posttussive emesis; infants may present with apnea and cyanosis without a whoop.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Unvaccinated/undervaccinated children, waning immunity in adolescents/adults, infected household contacts
Young infants have greatest risk of severe disease; vaccinated individuals can still transmit infection

rows.label: Clues
items: Catarrhal stage: rhinorrhea, mild cough, little or no fever; greatest early infectiousness
Inspiratory whoop often absent in adolescents/adults; convalescence can last weeks with recurrent cough
★ Infant **marked lymphocytosis**, poor feeding, or respiratory compromise; minimal fever despite serious illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: B. pertussis adheres to respiratory cilia; toxin-mediated injury impairs mucus clearance
Pertussis toxin inhibits Gi signaling; impaired lymphocyte extravasation causes circulating lymphocytosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Nasopharyngeal PCR** during first 3–4 weeks of cough; posterior nasopharynx, not throat swab
Culture most useful in first 2 weeks; late illness → validated serology when available
Treat suspected high-risk cases before results; chest imaging for respiratory compromise or suspected pneumonia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Azithromycin** preferred; TMP-SMX alternative at age ≥2 months when macrolides unsuitable
Best symptom benefit early; later treatment mainly reduces transmission within infectious window
Treat age ≥1 year within 3 weeks of cough; infants/pregnancy up to 6 weeks
Hospitalize young infants or apnea/hypoxemia; oxygen, suction, hydration and cardiorespiratory monitoring
Infant macrolides carry pyloric stenosis risk, but benefit outweighs risk; monitor vomiting

rows.label: Complications
items: Pneumonia, seizures/encephalopathy, infant pulmonary hypertension and death
Adults: rib fractures, syncope, stress incontinence from forceful coughing

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Droplet isolation until **5 days of effective antibiotics**, or 21 days from cough onset untreated
Household contacts → azithromycin prophylaxis within 21 days of index cough; also target high-risk exposures
DTaP childhood series; Tdap adolescent booster and once for adults without prior Tdap
★ **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 weeks**, preferably early in that interval

rows.label: Mimics
items: Viral bronchitis: improving ordinary cough without characteristic paroxysms or epidemiologic link
Asthma: recurrent wheeze/trigger pattern, reversible airflow obstruction
Chlamydial infant pneumonia: afebrile staccato cough, eosinophilia, often prior conjunctivitis

phobias.name: Phobias
phobias.scope: Specific phobia (flying, heights, blood-injection-injury), exposure therapy, situational benzodiazepines, social anxiety disorder (generalized vs performance-only), beta-blockers, agoraphobia
phobias.core: Persistent disproportionate fear leads to avoidance or endurance with intense distress, producing impairment despite recognition that danger is limited.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Temperamental inhibition, family anxiety, frightening experiences or learned fear; often childhood/adolescent onset

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Fear reliably provoked by trigger; duration **≥6 months**, excessive relative to actual/cultural danger
Anticipatory anxiety and avoidance limit school, work, medical care or travel
Blood-injection-injury subtype may produce vasovagal syncope rather than persistent tachycardia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Conditioned threat response and avoidance prevent extinction; relief from escape reinforces fear

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical assessment** of trigger, feared consequence, avoidance and impairment
Agoraphobia: fear in ≥2 categories—transport, open/enclosed spaces, crowds/lines, outside home alone
Exclude substances, hyperthyroidism, arrhythmia or pulmonary disease when bodily symptoms atypical
Symptoms only with feared trigger, normal exam → psychiatric evaluation, not pheochromocytoma/Holter workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Graded exposure-based CBT** first-line across phobic disorders
Blood-injection-injury: applied muscle tension during exposure reduces fainting
Generalized social anxiety: CBT or sertraline/escitalopram; venlafaxine alternative
★ Performance-only social anxiety → situational **propranolol**; asthma/bradycardia → short-acting benzodiazepine instead
Rare trigger (flight, MRI) → short-acting benzodiazepine (**↑GABA-A**); routine use risks dependence, impairs exposure

rows.label: Complications
items: Social/occupational restriction, depression, substance misuse; avoidance of necessary health care
Beta-blocker hypotension; benzodiazepine sedation, falls, impaired driving

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early treatment, repeated graduated practice and reduced avoidance help maintain gains
Avoid self-medication with alcohol; include relapse-prevention exposure plans

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: recurrent unexpected attacks; fear of further attacks
OCD: intrusive obsessions and rituals drive avoidance
Avoidant personality: pervasive longstanding inadequacy/rejection sensitivity, often coexists with social anxiety

phobias.evidence: Social anxiety care checked 2026-10-30: [NIMH](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/social-anxiety-disorder-more-than-just-shyness); established exposure-based care.

pleural-effusion.name: Pleural effusion
pleural-effusion.scope: Transudate vs exudate (Light criteria), parapneumonic effusion, empyema, malignant effusion
pleural-effusion.core: Fluid in the pleural space causes dyspnea, dullness, and reduced breath sounds; classify by mechanism and identify infection requiring drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome; pneumonia, malignancy, pulmonary embolism, TB
Recent thoracic surgery, pancreatitis, esophageal rupture, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Pleuritic pain, reduced fremitus; large effusion shifts mediastinum away; unilateral + cancer history → malignant
Fever or persistent sepsis despite antibiotics suggests complicated parapneumonic fluid/empyema
Bloody fluid: malignancy (prior cancer, mediastinal mass), embolism, trauma; milky → chyle
Foul-smelling pus after aspiration → **anaerobic empyema**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transudate: altered hydrostatic/oncotic pressure; exudate: increased permeability or impaired lymphatic drainage
Heart-failure transudate: pleural protein <3 g/dL, low LDH and cell count; **glucose equals serum**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Chest radiograph → **ultrasound-guided thoracentesis** for new unexplained, unilateral, or atypical effusion
Classic bilateral heart-failure effusions → diuresis first; sample if fever, asymmetry, or treatment failure
★ **Exudate if any Light criterion** positive; compare paired pleural and serum measurements
Pleural pH, glucose, cell differential, Gram stain/culture; cytology if cancer suspected
Diuresis can create pseudoexudate; serum–pleural albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL supports transudate

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat systemic cause; therapeutic thoracentesis for significant symptoms; avoid rapid excessive drainage
★ Pus, positive Gram stain/culture, **pH <7.20** or glucose <60 → empyema/complicated: chest tube, antibiotics
Loculated infected fluid → intrapleural tPA/DNase; persistent sepsis → VATS evaluation
★ Recurrent symptomatic malignancy → **indwelling pleural catheter** or pleurodesis; trapped lung favors catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, loculation, trapped lung, respiratory compromise
Thoracentesis → pneumothorax, bleeding, reexpansion pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Heart-failure control, prompt pneumonia treatment; ultrasound guidance reduces procedural injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atelectasis: mediastinal shift toward volume loss
Consolidation: increased fremitus, bronchial breath sounds
Pneumothorax: hyperresonance rather than dullness

pleural-effusion.evidence: Not checked online; established pleural disease teaching.

pneumothorax.name: Pneumothorax
pneumothorax.scope: Spontaneous pneumothorax (primary, secondary), tension pneumothorax, needle decompression, chest tube thoracostomy
pneumothorax.core: Pleural air causes acute unilateral pleuritic pain and reduced breath sounds; circulatory compromise indicates tension physiology requiring immediate decompression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Primary: tall thin young adults, smoking, family history
Secondary: COPD, cystic fibrosis, PJP, interstitial lung disease; trauma/procedures or positive-pressure ventilation

rows.label: Clues
items: Unilateral hyperresonance, dyspnea, asymmetric chest expansion; severity depends on underlying reserve
★ **Hypotension + distended neck veins + unilateral absent breath sounds** → tension; tracheal deviation is late
Ventilated: positive pressure converts occult pneumothorax to tension; sudden desaturation, rising airway pressure, collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Loss of negative pleural pressure permits lung collapse
One-way air entry increases intrathoracic pressure, reducing venous return and causing obstructive shock

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Unstable tension suspicion → **clinical diagnosis; no imaging delay**
Stable → upright chest radiograph: visceral pleural line with absent peripheral markings
Bedside ultrasound: absent sliding/B-lines supports; lung point highly specific; absent sliding alone nonspecific
CT for uncertain/complex cases; supine radiograph may show deep sulcus rather than apical air

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tension → **immediate needle or finger thoracostomy**, then chest tube; oxygen and resuscitation
Needle commonly fourth/fifth intercostal space anterior/midaxillary, or second midclavicular; insert above rib
★ Minimal symptoms, stable: primary (any size) or small iatrogenic → **observation**, reliable follow-up
Symptomatic/large primary → aspiration or small-bore chest tube; secondary generally admit, drain if symptomatic/significant
Persistent air leak, recurrence, bilateral disease, or high-risk occupation → VATS bleb treatment/pleurodesis

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure, tension progression, recurrence; reexpansion pulmonary edema after drainage
Chest tube → bleeding, infection, organ injury; blocked/clamped drain may recreate tension

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**; avoid flying until radiographic resolution and clearance
Scuba diving contraindicated without specialist assessment/definitive prevention; counsel recurrence warning symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: PE: pleuritic pain with preserved lung sliding, embolic risk
Giant bulla: intraparenchymal thin wall; CT if stable uncertainty before tube
Tamponade: shock with pericardial fluid rather than unilateral absent ventilation
Massive hemothorax: dullness, collapsed neck veins rather than distended

pneumothorax.evidence: Conservative care checked 2026-10-30: [BTS pleural guideline 2023](https://doi.org/10.1136/thorax-2022-219784); tension rescue: established emergency teaching.

population-health-and-quality-improvemen.name: Population health and quality improvement
population-health-and-quality-improvemen.scope: Program evaluation, outcome and process measures, health equity, PDSA cycles
population-health-and-quality-improvemen.core: Improve care for a defined population through measurable aims, iterative system changes, and attention to unequal access and outcomes.

rows.label: Principle
items: Population denominator includes eligible people missing visits, not only those receiving care
Equity: stratify outcomes by language, race/ethnicity, geography, disability, insurance, deprivation
Greater relative **primary care investment** improves population health, reduces disparities

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Define **measurable aim**, population, baseline, timeframe; engage patients/frontline staff
★ **PDSA**: plan small change → do → study results → act/adapt before scaling
Stratify measures, address interpreter/transport/cost barriers, monitor unintended consequences

rows.label: Don't
items: Do not assume a favorable outcome proves causation without comparison and context
Avoid blaming individuals for failures created by unreliable workflows

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Run/control charts distinguish routine common-cause variation from special-cause signals over time
Program evaluation: reach, fidelity, effectiveness, cost, sustainability versus original goals
Education program → measure knowledge/behavior change; small cohort cannot detect morbidity/mortality

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Process success ≠ patient benefit**; assess both and choose valid denominators
★ **Risk adjustment** improves comparison; also report disparities so adjustment cannot conceal inequity
Before–after improvement may reflect secular trends, case-mix change, regression to mean

population-health-and-quality-improvemen.evidence: Established quality-improvement and program-evaluation principles; no guideline-dependent thresholds.

potassium-disorders.name: Potassium disorders
potassium-disorders.scope: Hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, cardiac membrane stabilization, shift therapy, elimination
potassium-disorders.core: Potassium abnormalities can cause weakness and fatal arrhythmias; stabilize cardiac risk while identifying the cause and correcting total-body balance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hyperkalemia: AKI/CKD, RAAS blockers, potassium-sparing diuretics, tissue lysis, insulin deficiency
Hypokalemia: GI losses, loop/thiazide diuretics, hyperaldosteronism, insulin/beta-agonists, magnesium depletion

rows.label: Clues
items: Flaccid weakness, paralysis, palpitations; symptoms may be absent despite dangerous levels
★ **K ≥6.5 mmol/L, ECG changes, or rapid rise** → emergency; normal ECG not reassuring
Bradycardia/high-degree AV block with renal failure → suspect hyperkalemia; calcium before pacemaker

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Extracellular K changes alter membrane excitability and cardiac conduction
Acidosis/insulin deficiency shift K outward; intracellular shifts can coexist with severe total-body depletion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG + repeat potassium**, creatinine, glucose, bicarbonate, magnesium; assess drugs and acid-base status
Hemolysis, thrombocytosis/leukocytosis → pseudohyperkalemia; repeat atraumatic draw if clinically compatible
Hypokalemia: urine K distinguishes renal wasting from extrarenal loss; interpret with BP/acid-base pattern
Do not delay treatment for confirmatory blood draw when malignant ECG changes present

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hyperkalemic ECG changes or dialysis-patient arrest → **IV calcium gluconate/chloride first**; protects myocardium only
★ Shift K inward: **IV insulin + dextrose**, nebulized albuterol; bicarbonate mainly with significant acidosis
Remove K: loop diuretic if urine output, selected binders; urgent dialysis for severe refractory/renal-failure cases
Mild/stable hypokalemia → oral KCl; <2.5, arrhythmia, paralysis, or no oral access → monitored IV replacement
★ **Correct magnesium deficiency** for refractory low K; never give IV potassium push; monitor glucose after insulin

rows.label: Complications
items: Ventricular arrhythmia, cardiac arrest, respiratory muscle failure
Overcorrection, rebound dyskalemia; insulin-induced hypoglycemia; IV potassium extravasation/phlebitis
Diuretic hypokalemia → **digoxin toxicity**, multifocal PVCs; check K first

rows.label: Prevention
items: Review supplements/salt substitutes; monitor K/creatinine after diuretic or RAAS-drug changes
Treat diarrhea/vomiting and underlying mineralocorticoid disorders; replace ongoing losses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Guillain-Barré: ascending areflexic weakness without explanatory electrolyte pattern
Periodic paralysis: episodic shifts, sometimes thyrotoxicosis; avoid excessive replacement causing rebound

table.title: ECG patterns
rows: Peaked T → PR prolongation → wide QRS/sine-wave
Flat T, ST depression, prominent U waves

potassium-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established electrolyte emergency principles.

pressure-injuries.name: Pressure injuries
pressure-injuries.scope: Stage 1 through 4 pressure injuries, unstageable eschar, risk assessment (Braden scale), pressure offloading, repositioning, wound debridement, dressing selection
pressure-injuries.core: Sustained pressure and shear damage skin and deeper tissue over bony prominences or beneath medical devices.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobility, spinal cord injury, impaired sensation, poor perfusion, malnutrition
Moisture/incontinence, friction, advanced age; oxygen tubing and immobilization devices create focal loading

rows.label: Clues
items: Sacrum, heels, ischial tuberosities, occiput and device contact sites; pain may precede visible injury
Dark skin: assess temperature, induration and discoloration rather than redness alone
Purulence, spreading erythema, fever or worsening pain → infection; exposed bone raises osteomyelitis concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Capillary compression and tissue deformation → ischemia/reperfusion damage; shear increases deep injury
Surface appearance may underestimate muscle injury; stages describe depth, not a required progression

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Inspect skin and document depth**, drainage, undermining and surrounding tissue
Braden scale assesses sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition and friction/shear
Suspected osteomyelitis → MRI and, when feasible, bone biopsy/culture; superficial swabs poorly specific
Healing lesions retain their original highest stage; **never reverse-stage**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Offload pressure**, support surfaces and individualized repositioning; float heels with pillows under calves
Saline cleansing; shallow/low-exudate → hydrocolloid; draining → foam/alginate; maintain moisture, protect surrounding skin
★ Necrotic tissue → debridement, except **stable dry heel/ischemic eschar** without infection
Systemic antibiotics only for cellulitis, sepsis or osteomyelitis; not colonization alone
Deep defects → **oral protein/calorie supplements** if malnourished, not parenteral; then negative-pressure, flap closure

rows.label: Complications
items: Cellulitis, osteomyelitis, sepsis, chronic pain and functional decline

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Daily skin checks, mobilization, moisture barriers and adequate protein/calories
Avoid donut cushions, massage over prominences; reassess device fit and risk whenever clinical status changes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incontinence dermatitis: diffuse superficial moisture-associated damage, not focal loading
Arterial ulcer: distal ischemic site, weak pulses

table.title: Stage by visible depth
rows: Partial thickness; exposed dermis or serum blister
Full thickness; fat visible; no deep structures
Exposed/palpable fascia, muscle, tendon or bone
Persistent maroon/purple discoloration or blood blister

primary-immunodeficiencies.name: Primary immunodeficiencies
primary-immunodeficiencies.scope: Selective IgA deficiency, common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), X-linked agammaglobulinemia, severe combined immunodeficiency, hyper-IgE syndrome, Wiskott-Aldrich, chronic granulomatous disease
primary-immunodeficiencies.core: Recurrent, unusually severe, persistent, or opportunistic infections; organism pattern and age of onset localize the immune defect.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Consanguinity, affected relatives, male relatives dying in infancy; absent family history does not exclude disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, persistent thrush, or infections across multiple organ systems
Deep abscesses suggest phagocyte dysfunction; recurrent encapsulated bacteria suggest impaired antibody function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Selective IgA deficiency: impaired mucosal defense; respiratory infections, giardiasis, atopy, or no symptoms
Antibody disorders impair opsonization; T-cell defects permit viral, fungal, and protozoal opportunists
DiGeorge: 3rd/4th **pharyngeal pouch** failure → absent thymus, hypocalcemia, conotruncal defects, T-cell infections
ADA deficiency: autosomal recessive SCID; toxic deoxyadenosine destroys T and B cells

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Start **CBC with differential, quantitative immunoglobulins**, HIV testing; assess vaccine antibody responses
Lymphocyte subsets distinguish B-cell and T-cell deficiencies; abnormal results → genetic confirmation
IgA deficiency: isolated IgA <7 mg/dL after age 4 years; normal IgG and IgM
★ Newborn **TREC screen** detects impaired T-cell production before symptomatic SCID

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Profound combined immune failure → isolation, irradiated CMV-negative blood products, urgent **transplant evaluation**
Acute infections: organism-directed antimicrobials; immunoglobulin replacement not useful for isolated IgA deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Bronchiectasis, chronic enteropathy, autoimmune disease; CVID additionally increases lymphoma risk
Anti-IgA antibodies can cause anaphylaxis to blood products

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Avoid **live vaccines** in major T-cell defects; immunize household contacts with safe vaccine choices
IgA-related transfusion reactions → washed cellular products or IgA-deficient plasma
CGD: TMP-SMX + itraconazole prophylaxis; genetic counseling for inherited defects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vertical HIV: bacterial infections + zoster, nodes, maternal opportunistic infection; low CD4, positive virologic testing
Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia: nephrotic protein loss, B-cell malignancy, or rituximab exposure

table.title: Defect fingerprints
rows: Adolescent/adult; low IgG, poor vaccine response
Boy after 6 months; absent tonsils/B cells
Infant; absent thymic shadow, profound lymphopenia
Cold abscesses, eczema, retained teeth, pneumatoceles

primary-immunodeficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical immunology teaching.

psoriasis.name: Psoriasis
psoriasis.scope: Plaque psoriasis, nail pitting and onycholysis, Auspitz sign, Koebner phenomenon, psoriatic arthritis, topical and systemic therapy
psoriasis.core: Sharply demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale, usually on extensor surfaces or scalp; inspect nails and screen for inflammatory arthritis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, obesity, smoking, alcohol; stress, trauma, streptococcal infection
Lithium, beta blockers, antimalarials; systemic glucocorticoid withdrawal can trigger severe rebound

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Nail pitting, onycholysis**, oil-drop discoloration support diagnosis
Auspitz sign: pinpoint bleeding after scale removal; Koebner phenomenon: lesions at trauma sites
Psoriatic arthritis: morning stiffness, DIP disease, dactylitis, enthesitis, asymmetric or axial involvement
Generalized pustules, erythroderma, fever, hemodynamic disturbance → urgent evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-mediated TNF/IL-23/Th17 activation → accelerated keratinocyte turnover

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; biopsy if atypical; assess body surface area and functional impact
KOH scraping if fungal infection possible; inflammatory joint symptoms warrant rheumatology assessment
Before biologics: TB, hepatitis screening; before methotrexate: CBC, liver and renal tests, pregnancy assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized plaques → **topical corticosteroid + calcipotriene**; choose potency by site
Face/folds: low-potency steroid briefly or tacrolimus; emollients and scale removal aid penetration
★ Extensive/refractory disease → **narrowband UVB**, methotrexate, or targeted biologic; arthritis requires systemic control
Methotrexate contraindicated in pregnancy and significant liver disease; cyclosporine useful for rapid short-term control
Avoid routine systemic steroids; unstable erythrodermic/pustular disease → hospital support and specialist treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Joint destruction, depression, cardiometabolic disease; severe skin failure → fluid loss and infection
Systemic immunosuppression → infections; methotrexate → hepatotoxicity, marrow suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, weight management, limit alcohol; screen BP, lipids, diabetes, depression; reduce skin trauma

rows.label: Mimics
items: Tinea corporis: annular advancing edge, positive KOH
Seborrheic dermatitis: greasy scale in sebaceous areas
Atopic dermatitis: flexural eczema with marked pruritus

psoriasis.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatology and psoriatic arthritis teaching.

pubertal-development.name: Pubertal development
pubertal-development.scope: Tanner stages, normal thelarche vs breast mass, premature adrenarche, precocious puberty, constitutional delay of growth and puberty
pubertal-development.core: Interpret sexual maturation by sequence, age, growth velocity, and bone age; isolated benign variants lack progressive gonadal activation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constitutional delay often familial; chronic illness, undernutrition, excess exercise delay maturation
CNS lesions, gonadal/adrenal hormone excess, exogenous sex steroids can cause early puberty

rows.label: Clues
items: Girls: breast budding precedes peak growth, then menarche about 2–3 years later
Boys: testes enlarge before penile growth; pubic hair reflects adrenarche, not necessarily gonadarche
★ Asymmetric tender **subareolar breast bud** at expected age usually normal; hard eccentric mass needs evaluation
Rapid height acceleration, advancing secondary characteristics, neurologic symptoms → pathologic early maturation concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Central puberty: hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility → LH/FSH → gonadal steroids
Adrenarche produces adrenal androgens independently; peripheral hormone excess suppresses pituitary gonadotropins
Immature hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis → irregular anovulatory cycles, normal for 2–3 years after menarche
Virilized boy with **prepubertal testes** → peripheral androgen, usually adrenal; central puberty enlarges testes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Precocious: secondary sexual development **before 8 years girls or 9 years boys**
★ Delayed: **no breasts by 13**, no testes ≥4 mL by 14; evaluate absent menarche by 15
Growth chart, Tanner examination, bone age; LH/FSH, estradiol/testosterone, TSH selected by pattern
Central precocity → pubertal basal/stimulated LH; brain MRI especially boys, young girls, neurologic signs
Peripheral pattern → targeted adrenal/gonadal tests/imaging; isolated adrenarche requires exclusion of rapid virilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Progressive central precocity → **GnRH agonist**; treat CNS cause when present
Peripheral precocity → remove hormone source or treat tumor/adrenal disorder; GnRH agonist alone ineffective
Constitutional delay → reassurance, follow growth; distress → specialist-guided brief sex-steroid course
Benign premature thelarche/adrenarche → observe progression; no automatic hormonal treatment
Pubertal gynecomastia, unilateral or bilateral, smooth subareolar → **reassurance**; no labs/biopsy; carcinoma very rare

rows.label: Complications
items: Early epiphyseal closure → reduced adult height; psychosocial distress
Missed hypogonadism → impaired bone accrual; untreated CNS/tumor cause may progress

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, manage chronic disease, avoid household hormone exposure; serial growth surveillance
Normal puberty + moodiness, mild parent conflict → **puberty education** for child, parents; no drug testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary gonadal failure: high LH/FSH, low sex steroids
Permanent central hypogonadism: absent progression rather than eventual familial catch-up
Familial short stature: short parents, bone age matches chronologic age; constitutional delay: **delayed bone age**

table.title: Tanner staging anchors
rows: Further enlargement; menarche usually within 1–2 years

pubertal-development.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric endocrine timing and Tanner staging.

research-ethics.name: Research ethics
research-ethics.scope: Institutional review board (IRB), vulnerable populations (prisoners, children), coercion and undue inducement, clinical equipoise, informed consent in research
research-ethics.core: Scientifically valid research requires independent oversight, fair selection, favorable risk-benefit balance, and voluntary informed participation with additional safeguards for vulnerability.

rows.label: Principle
items: Respect for persons, beneficence, justice: autonomy, minimize harm, equitable recruitment
★ **Clinical equipoise**: expert uncertainty about superior treatment; personal doubt insufficient
Vulnerability warrants safeguards, not automatic exclusion from scientifically justified studies

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **IRB approval before recruitment**; disclose conflicts, monitor harms, report unexpected problems
Explain purpose, randomization, risks, uncertain benefits, alternatives, privacy, injury care, contacts
★ **Ongoing consent**: check understanding, answer questions, update risks; withdrawal without penalty

rows.label: Don't
items: Coercion: threaten lost care, employment, grades, liberty for refusal; parole offer to prisoners
Undue influence: incentives distort voluntary judgment; reasonable reimbursement/payment permitted
Placebo causing serious harm by withholding proven care; disguise research as personalized treatment

rows.label: Exceptions
items: IRB waiver: minimal risk, impracticable otherwise, preserved rights/welfare; later disclosure when needed
Identifiable-data waiver: study also impracticable without identifiers
Emergency research: prior regulatory safeguards/approval; treatment emergency exception insufficient

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **IRB approval never replaces informed consent** unless an authorized waiver applies
Capable child's dissent generally respected despite parental permission
Therapeutic misconception: participant assumes every study decision maximizes personal clinical benefit

table.title: Additional safeguards
rows: Parental permission plus developmentally capable child's assent
Permitted research category; prisoner representative on IRB
Legally authorized representative; seek participant assent

rickets.name: Rickets
rickets.scope: Nutritional vitamin D deficiency, X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets, metaphyseal cupping and fraying, elevated alkaline phosphatase, low phosphate, high PTH
rickets.core: Growing child with bowed legs, widened wrists, and delayed growth: evaluate defective growth-plate mineralization rather than treating the deformity alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ Nutritional: **unsupplemented breastfeeding**, low dietary calcium, limited sunlight, darker skin, malabsorption
Inherited phosphate wasting: X-linked dominant; affected fathers transmit to all daughters, no sons

rows.label: Clues
items: Rachitic rosary, craniotabes, delayed fontanelle closure, bone pain, hypotonia, delayed walking
Hypocalcemic tetany, seizures, prolonged QT, cardiomyopathy → urgent stabilization
Persistent short stature, lower-limb deformity, dental abscesses despite adequate vitamin D → phosphate-wasting disorder

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nutritional deficiency → reduced intestinal calcium absorption → secondary hyperparathyroidism and renal phosphate loss
**PHEX mutation → excess FGF23**, renal phosphaturia and inappropriately low calcitriol

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Wrist/knee radiograph → **metaphyseal cupping, fraying, widened growth plates**
★ Check **calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, PTH, 25-OH vitamin D**, creatinine; ALP elevated, phosphate reduced
25-OH vitamin D <12 ng/mL supports deficiency; interpret with calcium intake and biochemical pattern
Normal vitamin D with hypophosphatemia → assess renal phosphate wasting; genetic evaluation if inherited pattern

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic hypocalcemia → **IV calcium gluconate with ECG monitoring**, then oral calcium
During repletion → repeat calcium/phosphate/ALP; assess radiographic healing
Burosumab must not accompany oral phosphate/active vitamin D; specialist monitoring prevents excess phosphate
Persistent renal disease/acidosis → treat cause; orthopedic correction only for residual deformity after metabolic control

rows.label: Complications
items: Fractures, permanent deformity, impaired growth; severe hypocalcemia → arrhythmia
Phosphate/calcitriol: ↑PTH, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis → urine calcium and renal ultrasound monitoring

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Infants: **vitamin D 400 IU/day**; after 12 months, total intake 600 IU/day plus calcium-rich foods
Maternal nutrition, supplementation during malabsorption, and family counseling for inherited disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Physiologic bowing: symmetric toddler legs, normal growth plates/laboratory studies
Blount disease: focal medial tibial growth disturbance, often obesity; normal mineral studies
Osteogenesis imperfecta: fragile collagen, blue sclerae; no characteristic growth-plate changes

sarcoidosis.name: Sarcoidosis
sarcoidosis.scope: Noncaseating granulomas, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, pulmonary infiltrates, hypercalcemia, extrapulmonary manifestations (uveitis, erythema nodosum, neurosarcoidosis, cardiac), systemic corticosteroids
sarcoidosis.core: Multisystem granulomatous disease, classically a young adult with bilateral hilar adenopathy; treat threatened organ function rather than an abnormal radiograph alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young or middle-aged adults; higher prevalence and disease burden among Black Americans
Familial predisposition; environmental antigen exposure suspected, without one established infectious cause

rows.label: Clues
items: Dry cough, exertional dyspnea; restrictive physiology and ↓DLCO; upper-lung interstitial infiltrates
★ **Löfgren syndrome**: erythema nodosum + ankle arthritis + hilar adenopathy; usually favorable prognosis
Uveitis, lupus pernio, parotid enlargement; facial palsy, hypothalamic dysfunction suggest neurosarcoidosis
★ Unexplained **AV block, ventricular arrhythmia, syncope** → cardiac involvement

rows.label: Pathophys
items: CD4-mediated granulomas; macrophage 1α-hydroxylase → ↑calcitriol, hypercalcemia/hypercalciuria, suppressed PTH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Chest radiograph**, PFTs; baseline calcium, creatinine, liver tests, ECG and eye examination
Compatible presentation + **noncaseating granulomas** + exclusion of TB/fungi/beryllium exposure
Sample accessible lesion or EBUS-guided hilar/mediastinal node; classic Löfgren presentation may avoid biopsy
ACE level neither sensitive nor specific; cardiac symptoms/ECG abnormalities → cardiac MRI ± FDG-PET

rows.label: Tx
items: Asymptomatic stage I disease, preserved function → observation with clinical/PFT follow-up
★ **Prednisone** for progressive symptomatic pulmonary disease, significant hypercalcemia, cardiac or neurologic disease
Uveitis → urgent ophthalmology, topical or systemic corticosteroids according to severity
Steroid-dependent disease → methotrexate; refractory organ-threatening disease → specialist-directed infliximab
Hypercalcemia → hydration; restrict excess calcium/vitamin D and sunlight exposure

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary fibrosis, pulmonary hypertension, respiratory failure; nephrolithiasis and kidney injury
Cardiomyopathy, sudden death; visual loss; chronic steroids → infection, osteoporosis, diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: No established primary prevention; smoking cessation and vaccination reduce respiratory morbidity
Monitor treatment toxicity and bone health; individualize vitamin D replacement because calcitriol may already be elevated

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal infection: organisms or positive microbiology; exclude before immunosuppression
Berylliosis: aerospace/industrial exposure, positive beryllium lymphocyte proliferation test
Lymphoma: malignant tissue, constitutional symptoms; granulomas alone do not exclude concurrent cancer

schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.name: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.scope: Brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, mesolimbic dopamine
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.core: Psychosis with impaired reality testing: distinguish schizophrenia-spectrum disorders by duration, functional decline, and the relationship between mood episodes and psychosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, neurodevelopmental vulnerability; adolescent cannabis exposure increases risk
Typical onset late adolescence/early adulthood; exclude stimulant, hallucinogen, medication, and neurologic causes

rows.label: Clues
items: Delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech/behavior; negative symptoms: avolition, alogia, flat affect
★ At least **two core symptoms**, including delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech, for active-phase diagnosis
Suicidality, dangerous commands or inability to eat → urgent safety assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **↑Mesolimbic dopamine** → positive symptoms; mesocortical → negative symptoms, early working-memory deficits
D2 blockade reduces psychosis but nigrostriatal/tuberoinfundibular effects cause EPS and hyperprolactinemia
Structural correlate: **enlarged lateral and third ventricles**, reduced cortical volume

rows.label: Dx
items: Clinical history, collateral information, mental status; assess mood timeline and substance exposure
First episode → CBC/CMP, TSH, toxicology; HIV/syphilis or neuroimaging for relevant risks/atypical neurologic findings
★ **Schizoaffective**: ≥2 weeks psychosis without mood episode; mood episodes occupy most illness duration

rows.label: Tx
items: Safety crisis → hospitalization; acute agitation → de-escalation, then medication if needed
★ **Risperidone, aripiprazole or olanzapine** + coordinated specialty care, family education, CBT, supported employment
Schizoaffective depressive/bipolar subtype → add antidepressant or mood stabilizer according to mood syndrome
★ Failure of two adequate antipsychotic trials or persistent substantial suicide risk → **clozapine**
Adherence difficulty → long-acting injectable (haloperidol decanoate); catatonia → lorazepam, then ECT if refractory

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, homelessness, substance use, cardiometabolic disease; antipsychotics → metabolic syndrome, tardive dyskinesia, NMS
Clozapine → neutropenia, myocarditis, severe constipation; monitor ANC and symptoms

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid cannabis/stimulants; maintenance medication, relapse planning reduce recurrence
Monitor weight, BP, glucose, lipids; address tobacco use and cardiovascular risk
**High expressed emotion** (family criticism, hostility) → relapse; family therapy reduces recurrence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mood disorder with psychosis: psychosis occurs exclusively during mood episodes
Delirium: fluctuating attention/awareness and acute medical cause
Delusional disorder: ≥1 month delusions with otherwise relatively preserved function, limited other psychotic symptoms
Substance/medication-induced psychosis: recent stimulants (mydriasis, tremor) or corticosteroids, intact orientation

secondary-hypertension.name: Secondary hypertension
secondary-hypertension.scope: Renal artery stenosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing syndrome, coarctation of aorta, diagnostic workup
secondary-hypertension.core: Abrupt, unusually young, severe, or resistant hypertension suggests a treatable secondary driver.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Renal stenosis: older smoker → atherosclerotic **lipid plaque**; young/middle-aged woman → **fibromuscular dysplasia** (medial hyperplasia, renal + carotid)
Renal disease, adrenal tumors, sleep apnea
NSAIDs, oral contraceptives, stimulants, glucocorticoids, licorice; medication nonadherence can mimic resistance

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hypokalemia + metabolic alkalosis** → aldosterone excess, primary or renovascular; normal K does not exclude it
**Abdominal bruit**, diffuse atherosclerosis, late abrupt worsening, small unilateral kidney → renal artery stenosis
Flash pulmonary edema or creatinine rise >30% after ACE inhibitor/ARB → renovascular disease
**Episodic headache, sweating, palpitations** → pheochromocytoma; cushingoid appearance, upper-body hypertension guide testing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Renal hypoperfusion → juxtaglomerular **renin** → RAAS; ACE inhibitor removes efferent constriction → ↓renal flow, ↓GFR across stenosis
Autonomous aldosterone → distal sodium absorption, potassium loss, low renin; pressure natriuresis escape prevents edema
Adrenal medullary catecholamine or cortisol excess, aortic obstruction, or nocturnal hypoxia increases vascular pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **home/ambulatory BP**, adherence, cuff technique; BMP, urinalysis, creatinine, TSH
Sleep-apnea symptoms → polysomnography; abnormal urinary sediment → renal ultrasound and kidney evaluation
★ Biochemical testing precedes adrenal imaging; correct hypokalemia and account for interfering medications
Endocrine Society 2025: suggest **aldosterone screening for all hypertension**, conditional on resources

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Primary aldosteronism: unilateral → **adrenalectomy**; bilateral → spironolactone/eplerenone
Renovascular atherosclerosis → medical risk reduction; revascularize selected recurrent pulmonary edema or refractory disease
Fibromuscular dysplasia → angioplasty; critical bilateral renal stenosis → avoid ACE inhibitor/ARB
★ Pheochromocytoma: **alpha blockade before beta blockade**, volume expansion, then surgery
Treat cortisol source, repair significant coarctation, use CPAP for OSA; stop contributing drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, heart failure, CKD, retinopathy
Unopposed alpha stimulation after beta blockade can cause catecholamine crisis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor renal function/K after RAAS blockers or mineralocorticoid antagonists
Genetic evaluation/family screening for suspected hereditary pheochromocytoma or congenital aortic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: normal out-of-office readings
Essential hypertension: gradual course without specific endocrine/renal clues

table.title: Targeted workup
rows: Selective suppression test; CT/adrenal venous sampling
Plasma free or urine fractionated metanephrines

secondary-hypertension.evidence: Aldosterone screening checked 2026-10-30: [Endocrine Society 2025](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/primary-aldosteronism-2); other causes: established teaching.

sickle-cell-disease.name: Sickle cell disease
sickle-cell-disease.scope: Vaso-occlusive pain crisis, acute chest syndrome, splenic sequestration, aplastic crisis, stroke, sickle cell trait, hemoglobin electrophoresis
sickle-cell-disease.core: HbS polymerization causes chronic hemolysis and episodic vascular occlusion; fever, hypoxemia and focal neurologic deficits require urgent escalation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive β-globin disease; dehydration, hypoxemia, cold and infection trigger sickling
Functional asplenia → encapsulated infection from early childhood; **S. pneumoniae** leads pneumonia and fulminant sepsis

rows.label: Clues
items: Baseline anemia, reticulocytosis, jaundice; childhood dactylitis or recurrent severe bone pain
Acute chest syndrome: **new pulmonary infiltrate** plus fever, respiratory symptoms or hypoxemia
Sequestration: sudden splenomegaly, falling hemoglobin, shock; aplasia: **low reticulocyte count**, often parvovirus

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Deoxygenated hemoglobin polymerizes → rigid erythrocytes, endothelial injury, ischemia and shortened RBC survival
Acute chest trigger: **infection** most common; in situ thrombosis and fat embolism less often
Severe anemia → low viscosity, vasodilation, ↓afterload → **↑cardiac output** preserves oxygen delivery

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Hemoglobin electrophoresis/HPLC confirms genotype; newborn screen detects disease before symptoms
Crisis → CBC, reticulocytes, bilirubin; fever → blood cultures; respiratory symptoms → chest radiograph
New focal deficit → emergency brain imaging, without delaying transfusion preparation
Distinguish osteomyelitis from infarction using cultures and MRI when focal fever/pain persists

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain crisis → prompt **IV opioid**, morphine (AKI: lower dose or hydromorphone); no meperidine; NSAID only if kidneys normal
Pain crisis support: euvolemic hydration; oxygen only for hypoxemia; no routine transfusion
★ Acute chest → oxygen, **ceftriaxone + azithromycin**, incentive spirometry; transfuse for significant anemia
Severe acute chest, stroke → **urgent exchange transfusion**; sequestration (cautious) or aplasia → simple transfusion
Fever → immediate **IV ceftriaxone/cefotaxime**, despite daily penicillin prophylaxis

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, avascular necrosis, priapism, pigment gallstones, nephropathy, retinopathy
Repeated transfusions → alloimmunization and iron overload; delayed hyperhemolysis can worsen anemia
Chronic hemolysis → ↑folate demand → **folate deficiency**, macrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hydroxyurea** raises HbF, reduces crises; monitor CBC
Penicillin prophylaxis through age 5 in HbSS; pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib and influenza vaccines
Annual transcranial Doppler ages 2–16 in HbSS/HbSβ0; abnormal → chronic transfusion program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: persistent localized pain, fever; Salmonella or S. aureus
Iron deficiency: low ferritin, no hemolytic pattern

skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.name: Skin and soft tissue infections
skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.scope: Cellulitis, erysipelas, folliculitis, furuncles, carbuncles, lymphangitis, necrotizing fasciitis
skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.core: Skin infection management depends on purulence, systemic illness, and signs of deep tissue destruction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Skin breaks, tinea pedis, edema/lymphedema, diabetes, obesity, injection drug use
Prior MRSA, crowding, recent hospitalization; surgery or penetrating trauma raises deep-infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Warmth, tenderness, erythema; rapidly expanding margins or systemic toxicity require urgent reassessment
★ **Pain out of proportion**, bullae, anesthesia, crepitus, shock → necrotizing infection
Perineal infection, especially diabetes → Fournier gangrene/necrotizing fasciitis; saltwater exposure → Vibrio, freshwater → Aeromonas

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nonpurulent infection usually streptococcal, S aureus possible; purulent lesions usually S aureus
Fascial spread, toxins → necrosis, sepsis; minor trauma, no crepitus → **GAS**; crepitus → Clostridium/polymicrobial
Tinea pedis = portal of entry: acute fever/cellulitis is bacterial (S aureus/streptococcal) superinfection, not Trichophyton

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical diagnosis; **bedside ultrasound** if occult fluid collection suspected
Culture drained pus for severe, recurrent, or resistant infection; blood cultures for systemic toxicity
Suspected necrotizing disease → immediate surgical evaluation; imaging must not delay exploration
Low laboratory risk score or absent gas does not exclude necrotizing fasciitis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Deep infection → **urgent debridement + vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam**, add clindamycin for toxin suppression
Confirmed group A streptococcal necrotizing infection → penicillin + clindamycin
Moderate cellulitis (systemic signs) → IV cefazolin; MRSA risk or cephalexin failure → vancomycin; severe → + pip-tazo
★ Abscess: add **antibiotics** for systemic signs, immunocompromise, extensive disease, or failed drainage
Pregnancy + suspected MRSA → clindamycin or vancomycin; **no doxycycline or fluoroquinolones**

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, osteomyelitis, septic thrombophlebitis; tissue loss and amputation
Toxic shock, multiorgan failure; recurrent cellulitis worsens lymphatic dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat interdigital fungal infection, manage edema, skin hygiene, protect wounds
Recurrent staphylococcal infections → consider nasal mupirocin + chlorhexidine decolonization; avoid shared razors

rows.label: Mimics
items: Stasis dermatitis: chronic, often bilateral, itchy
DVT: deep swelling without superficial spreading infection; contact dermatitis: pruritic exposure-pattern rash
Superficial thrombophlebitis: palpable indurated venous cord, not lymphatic streaks

table.title: Superficial patterns
rows: Incision and drainage; TMP-SMX if needed
Tender red streaks from skin break toward nodes
Usually S pyogenes; cephalexin; IV if systemic
Itchy follicular pustules on trunk/thighs after hot tub

skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.evidence: Not checked online; established IDSA-based infection management.

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → deep shave or punch biopsy; <1 cm → **narrow-margin excisional biopsy**
AK persisting after topical fluorouracil → **excisional biopsy** to exclude invasive SCC
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
Low-risk BCC → **excision with narrow margins (≤1 cm)**; no sentinel node biopsy
Positive margin on BCC/SCC → **reexcision** or Mohs, not observation
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
Advanced melanoma → specialist immunotherapy, selected BRAF-targeted drugs; avoid destructive treatment before diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: BCC: extensive local destruction, rare metastasis; SCC: nodal metastasis, especially high-risk sites/immunosuppression
Melanoma: distant metastases, including brain; immunotherapy → colitis, endocrinopathies, pneumonitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Broad-spectrum SPF ≥30**, reapply every 2 hours/outdoors after swimming; shade, protective clothing, no tanning
Infants <6 months → **shade, protective clothing**; avoid sunscreen
Self-examination, postcancer follow-up; suspicious lesions require evaluation despite uncertain population-screening benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seborrheic keratosis: waxy stuck-on plaque; atypical lesions still biopsy
Dermatofibroma: firm papule with dimple sign
Benign nevus: stable symmetric uniform, <6 mm → **observation**, even with melanoma family history
Congenital melanocytic nevus: brown lesion from birth, may darken or grow coarse hair

table.title: Nonmelanoma patterns
rows: Nonhealing scaly indurated plaque/ulcer/nodule; lip/ear common
Assess high-risk features and regional nodes
Pearly rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer
Treat despite slow growth; local invasion

skin-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAD melanoma guidance](https://www.aad.org/member/clinical-quality/guidelines/melanoma); established keratinocyte-cancer and photoprotection teaching.

solid-organ-transplantation.name: Solid organ transplantation
solid-organ-transplantation.scope: Hyperacute rejection, acute allograft rejection, chronic allograft rejection, immunosuppressive regimens
solid-organ-transplantation.core: Allograft dysfunction requires urgent distinction among rejection, infection, obstruction/vascular failure, and immunosuppressant toxicity; biopsy usually establishes the rejection mechanism.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HLA mismatch; sensitization after transplant, transfusion or pregnancy → preformed donor-specific antibodies
Missed immunosuppression, underdosing, drug interactions; rejection can occur late after medication withdrawal

rows.label: Clues
items: Kidney: ↑creatinine; liver: ↑bilirubin/enzymes; heart: ventricular dysfunction; lung: ↓spirometry
Fever, graft tenderness or malaise possible; rejection may be asymptomatic before laboratory abnormalities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allorecognition targets donor tissue; immunosuppression balances graft protection against infection and malignancy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Graft ultrasound/Doppler** when relevant → exclude obstruction, thrombosis or vascular compromise
Medication adherence/troughs, cultures and organ-specific viral testing; donor-specific antibodies assess humoral injury
★ **Allograft biopsy** distinguishes rejection from drug toxicity/infection; C4d may support antibody-mediated injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Common kidney maintenance: **tacrolimus + mycophenolate ± prednisone**; regimen varies by organ and risk
Induction in selected recipients → basiliximab or antithymocyte globulin
Steroid-resistant cellular rejection → antithymocyte globulin; coordinate all treatment with transplant team
Never reflexively escalate immunosuppression for unexplained fever before evaluating infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Calcineurin inhibitors → nephrotoxicity, hypertension, neurotoxicity; tacrolimus → diabetes
Mycophenolate → cytopenias, diarrhea, teratogenicity; sirolimus → poor wound healing, hyperlipidemia
Glucocorticoids → diabetes/osteoporosis; immunosuppression → opportunistic infection, skin cancer, EBV-related PTLD

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **ABO compatibility, HLA assessment, crossmatch** before transplant; lifelong adherence and trough monitoring
TMP-SMX prophylaxis for Pneumocystis; valganciclovir or preemptive monitoring for CMV according to risk
Vaccinate before transplant; avoid live vaccines during immunosuppression; sun protection and skin checks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Calcineurin toxicity: excessive exposure, no graft tenderness/enlargement; compatible biopsy, no alloimmune infiltrates
BK nephropathy: kidney transplant, viral PCR and viral inclusions on biopsy
Mechanical graft failure: obstruction/thrombosis demonstrated by imaging

table.title: Rejection patterns
rows: T-cell infiltrates; liver: portal eosinophils, endotheliitis

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.name: Stable ischemic heart disease
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.scope: Stable angina pectoris, exercise stress testing, stress echocardiography, antianginal pharmacotherapy, invasive coronary angiography indications
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.core: Predictable exertional chest pressure relieved by rest reflects myocardial oxygen supply–demand mismatch; new rest symptoms require acute coronary syndrome evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, older age, family history of premature CAD
Anemia, tachycardia, and uncontrolled blood pressure can worsen ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Substernal squeezing, arm/jaw radiation; dyspnea or exertional indigestion may be anginal equivalents
Normal resting ECG does not exclude CAD; examination often normal between episodes
★ **Crescendo symptoms, prolonged pain, rest pain**, instability → ECG/troponins and ACS pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Flow-limiting coronary atherosclerosis restricts supply when demand rises
Microvascular dysfunction can produce ischemia despite absence of obstructive epicardial disease

rows.label: Dx
items: Resting ECG, lipid profile, HbA1c, renal function; estimate clinical likelihood before choosing testing
★ Selected intermediate-risk suspected CAD → **CCTA or stress testing**, based on suitability
★ **Coronary angiography** for high-risk noninvasive findings, refractory limiting symptoms, or suspected high-risk anatomy
Stable on medical therapy, low-risk ischemia → no repeat testing or mandatory catheterization; respect informed refusal
Sedentary, risk factors, starting vigorous exercise: no routine stress test; older exam questions may expect exercise ECG

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Relief → **sublingual nitroglycerin**; avoid with recent PDE-5 inhibitor use or hypotension
★ Prevention → **aspirin + high-intensity statin**; manage BP/diabetes, lifestyle and exercise
Antianginal first-line: beta blocker or calcium-channel blocker; persistent symptoms → long-acting nitrate or ranolazine
